8	/-!
9	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
12	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
13	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
14	stabilized along the refinement preorder.
15	
16	## Main declarations
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
19	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
20	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
21	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
23	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
24	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
26	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
27	-/

41	/-! ## The Picard group  -/
42	
43	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
44	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
46	  iseqv := by
47	    constructor
48	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
50	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
51	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
52	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
53	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
54	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
55	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
56	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'
57	
58	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
59	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
60	def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
61	  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)
62	
63	namespace CechPic
64	
65	/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
66	def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
67	  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧
68	
69	@[elab_as_elim]
70	theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
71	    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
72	    motive x :=
73	  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x
74	
75	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
76	    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
77	      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
78	        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
79	  Quotient.eq
80	
81	/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
82	particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
83	@[simp]
84	theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
85	    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
86	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩
87	
88	private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
89	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
90	  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩
91	
92	private lemma mulSig_assoc {𝒰 𝒱 𝒳 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱)
93	    (c : X.unitsH1 𝒳) :
94	    mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳)
95	        (unitsRes inf_le_left (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) *
96	          unitsRes inf_le_right c)
97	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳))
98	        (unitsRes inf_le_left a *
99	          unitsRes inf_le_right (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right c)) := by
100	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳, le_rfl, (inf_assoc 𝒰 𝒱 𝒳).le, ?_⟩
101	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
102	  exact mul_assoc _ _ _
103	
104	private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
105	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
106	  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
107	  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
108	  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
109	  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
110	  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
111	  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf h₁ h₃, inf_le_inf h₂ h₄, ?_⟩
112	  show unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₁ h₃) (unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2)
113	      = unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₂ h₄) (unitsRes inf_le_left p'.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q'.2)
114	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
115	  rw [e₁', e₂']
116	
117	instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
118	  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
119	  one := mk ⊤ 1
120	  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by
121	    rintro p p' ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
122	    exact ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, by simp only [map_inv, e]⟩)
123	  mul_assoc a b c := by
124	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
125	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
126	    induction c using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒳 c =>
127	    exact mulSig_assoc a b c
128	  one_mul a := by
129	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
130	    show mk (⊤ ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤) * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
131	      = mk 𝒰 a
132	    rw [map_one, one_mul, mk_unitsRes]
133	  mul_one a := by
134	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
135	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ ⊤) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤))
136	      = mk 𝒰 a
137	    rw [map_one, mul_one, mk_unitsRes]
138	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
139	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
140	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left a⁻¹ * unitsRes inf_le_right a) = mk ⊤ 1
141	    have h : unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a⁻¹
142	        * unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰) a = 1 := by
143	      rw [map_inv]
144	      exact inv_mul_cancel _
145	    rw [h]
146	    exact Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
147	  mul_comm a b := by
148	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
149	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
150	    show mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b)
151	      = mk (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
152	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, le_rfl, le_inf inf_le_right inf_le_left, ?_⟩
153	    simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
154	    exact mul_comm _ _
155	
156	lemma one_def : (1 : X.CechPic) = mk ⊤ 1 :=
157	  rfl
158	
159	/-- Multiplication of Picard classes on representatives: restrict both to the common
160	refinement `𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱` and multiply there. Holds by definition. -/
161	lemma mk_mul_mk_inf {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱) :
162	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒱 b
163	      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	lemma mk_one (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : mk 𝒰 (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = 1 :=
168	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
169	
170	@[simp]
171	lemma mk_mul_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a b : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
172	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒰 b = mk 𝒰 (a * b) := by
173	  rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
174	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, inf_le_left, ?_⟩
175	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_rfl]
176	
177	@[simp]
178	lemma mk_inv (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : (mk 𝒰 a)⁻¹ = mk 𝒰 a⁻¹ :=
179	  rfl

181	/-! ## Functoriality: pullback of Picard classes -/
182	
183	private def mapSig (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
184	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
185	  ⟨p.1.pullback f, f.pullbackUnitsH1 p.1 p.2⟩
186	
187	private lemma mapSig_compat (f : X ⟶ Y) :
188	    ∀ {p q : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰}, p ≈ q → mapSig f p ≈ mapSig f q := by
189	  rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
190	  refine ⟨𝒲.pullback f, PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁,
191	    PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂, ?_⟩
192	  show unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
193	      = unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
194	  rw [Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₁ a, Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₂ b, e]
195	
196	/-- Contravariant functoriality of the Čech Picard group: pull the cover back pointwise,
197	pull the unit cocycles back through `f`, restrict. -/
198	def map (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic where
199	  toFun := Quotient.map (mapSig f) fun _ _ h ↦ mapSig_compat f h
200	  map_one' := by
201	    show mk ((⊤ : Y.PointedCover).pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 ⊤ 1) = 1
202	    rw [map_one, mk_one]
203	  map_mul' a b := by
204	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
205	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
206	    show mk ((𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f)
207	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b))
208	      = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) *
209	          mk (𝒱.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
210	    rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
211	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f, le_rfl,
212	      le_inf (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_left)
213	        (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_right), ?_⟩
214	    simp only [map_mul, ← Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
215	
216	@[simp]
217	lemma map_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (a : Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
218	    map f (mk 𝒰 a) = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) :=
219	  rfl
220	
221	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along the identity is the identity. -/
222	@[simp]
223	theorem map_id (X : Scheme.{u}) : map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id X.CechPic := by
224	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
225	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
226	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X)) ((𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) = mk 𝒰 a
227	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X) ≤ 𝒰 := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
228	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
229	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
230	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
231	  ext x y T a b
232	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
233	    γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf]
234	  exact id_unitsAppLE _ _
235	
236	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along a composite (the lane keystone). -/
237	theorem map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = (map f).comp (map g) := by
238	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
239	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
240	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g)) ((f ≫ g).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
241	    = mk ((𝒰.pullback g).pullback f)
242	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰.pullback g) (g.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a))
243	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g) ≤ (𝒰.pullback g).pullback f := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
244	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
245	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
246	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
247	  ext x y T a b
248	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
249	    Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE]
250	  rfl

252	/-! ## Sanity gate: triviality over a field -/
253	
254	/-- On a scheme with a subsingleton underlying space — e.g. `Spec` of a field — the
255	Čech Picard group is trivial: every pointed cover is a cover by a single open, on which
256	every unit cocycle is a coboundary. -/
257	instance subsingleton_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] :
258	    Subsingleton X.CechPic := by
259	  refine ⟨fun p q ↦ ?_⟩
260	  induction p using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
261	  induction q using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
262	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, inf_le_left, inf_le_right, ?_⟩
263	  have := H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
264	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens (fun i j ↦ le_of_eq (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim i j)))
265	  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
266	
267	/-- The Čech Picard group of the spectrum of a field is trivial. -/
268	theorem eq_one_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] (x : X.CechPic) :
269	    x = 1 :=
270	  Subsingleton.elim x 1
271	
272	example {K : Type u} [Field K] (x : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).CechPic) : x = 1 :=
273	  eq_one_of_subsingleton _ x

11	
12	The carrier assembly of the truncated-exponential Čech kernel on the Rebuild's pinned
13	two-cover section rings: for a scheme `X` over `Spec k` with two affine opens
14	`U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, write `B = Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)` for the overlap ring and
15	`ρᵢ = X.resHom : Γ(X, Uᵢ) →+* B` for the restrictions. Composing
16	
17	* the landed two-cover H¹ bridge `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv :
18	  H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`,
19	* the carrier translation `range diff = ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂)` (a difference and a sum of
20	  chart sections span the same additive subgroup — `range_diff_toAddSubgroup`), and
21	* the pure-algebra engine `TruncExpCech.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv :
22	  B ⧸ (ρ₁A₁ + ρ₂A₂) ≃+ Additive (ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)))`
23	
24	gives the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle-leg identification
25	
26	```
27	H¹(X, 𝒪_X)  ≃+  ker( Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)) )
28	```

30	(`TwoCover.h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel`), the two-cover Čech form of
31	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ ker(Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C))`. On generators it sends the connecting class
32	`delta s` of an overlap section to the class of the truncated exponential `1 + s ε`
33	(`h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta`, with the generator map bundled as
34	`TwoCover.truncExpClass`). For the challenge curve, instantiate at an
35	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover` of `C.left` (which exists:
36	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`); `Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
37	is definitionally the carrier whose `finrank` is `genus C`.
38	
39	**`k`-linearity interface (the D6/R5(iii) distributivity dodge).** The equivalence is
40	additive only, BY DESIGN: no `SMul k` is ever placed on the units-kernel side, so the
41	old draft's unproved `(a+b) • x` Mumford-scaling distributivity is never needed. The
42	`k`-action lives on the H¹/cokernel side, where it is the honest module structure, and

113	      = X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a :=
114	  X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op a
115	
116	/-- Restriction to the overlap intertwines the structure constants of the two charts:
117	`ρ₂ ∘ (k → Γ(U₁)) = (k → Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))`. -/
118	theorem resHom_overAlgebraMap_right (a : k) :
119	    X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁) (X.overAlgebraMap k U₁ a)
120	      = X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a :=
121	  X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op a
122	
123	/-! ## The Čech-units reduction of the two-cover -/
124	
125	/-- **The Čech-units reduction of the two-cover at the dual-number thickening**:
126	`Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))` for the two-chart datum of restriction ring
127	homomorphisms — the Čech-cocycle incarnation of the restriction
128	`Pic(X ×ₖ Spec k[ε]) → Pic(X)` along `ε ↦ 0`. Reducible wrapper
129	(`unitsReduction_def`) around `TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction`, naming the pinned
130	two-cover instance once (reducible so that all statements below unify transparently
131	with the engine's `cechUnitsReduction` spelling). Its kernel is computed from
132	`H¹(X, 𝒪)` by `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel` below. -/
133	noncomputable abbrev unitsReduction :
134	    ((Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
135	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
136	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) →*
137	      (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁))ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
138	        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
139	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
140	  cechUnitsReduction (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
141	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))
142	
143	/-- `unitsReduction` is `TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction` at the two-cover restriction
144	datum, definitionally. -/
145	theorem unitsReduction_def :
146	    unitsReduction X U₀ U₁
147	      = cechUnitsReduction (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
148	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
149	  rfl
150	
151	/-! ## The truncated-exponential kernel classes of overlap sections -/
152	
153	/-- **The truncated-exponential kernel class of an overlap section**: the class of the
154	unit `1 + b ε` in the kernel of the Čech-units reduction, written additively. This is
155	the generator map of the ε-kernel: `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel` sends the connecting
156	class `delta s` to `truncExpClass s`. -/
157	noncomputable def truncExpClass (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
158	    Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker :=
159	  Additive.ofMul (α := (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker)
160	    ⟨QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b),
161	      MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr
162	        (cechUnitsReduction_mk_truncExpUnit
163	          (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
164	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) b)⟩
165	
166	/-- **The underlying thickened Čech class of an element of the ε-kernel** — the
167	coercion `Additive (ker) → Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])` as a named map. Kernel discipline: one
168	opaque head for the coercion seam, so that rewriting under it never re-elaborates the
169	scheme-tower coercions (`kerVal_eq_coe` recovers the raw coercion). -/
170	noncomputable def kerVal (y : Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
171	    (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
172	      (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
173	      (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))) :=
174	  (Additive.toMul y : (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker).1
175	
176	/-- `kerVal` is the raw coercion, definitionally. -/
177	theorem kerVal_eq_coe (y : Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
178	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ y
179	      = ((Additive.toMul y : (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
180	          (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
181	            (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
182	            (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) :=
183	  rfl
184	
185	/-- The underlying thickened Čech class of `truncExpClass b` is `[1 + b ε]`.
186	Definitional. -/
187	theorem truncExpClass_val (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
188	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ (truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b) = QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :=
189	  rfl
190	
191	/-- `truncExpClass` is the truncated-exponential kernel engine applied to the residue
192	class of the section: `truncExpClass b = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv ρ₁ ρ₂ [b]`.
193	Definitional; the workhorse normal form for the lemmas below. -/
194	theorem truncExpClass_eq_engine (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
195	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b
196	      = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
197	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) (QuotientAddGroup.mk b) :=
198	  rfl
199	
200	/-- Additivity of the truncated-exponential kernel classes:
201	`(1 + bε)(1 + cε) = 1 + (b+c)ε`. -/
202	theorem truncExpClass_add (b c : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
203	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ (b + c)
204	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b + truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ c := by
205	  rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine X U₀ U₁ b, truncExpClass_eq_engine X U₀ U₁ c, ← map_add,
206	    ← QuotientAddGroup.mk_add, ← truncExpClass_eq_engine]
207	
208	/-- Vanishing of a truncated-exponential kernel class: `[1 + b ε] = 0` iff `b` is a
209	Čech coboundary `ρ₁ a₁ + ρ₂ a₂` of the two charts. -/
210	theorem truncExpClass_eq_zero_iff (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
211	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b = 0
212	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
213	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) := by
214	  rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine, EmbeddingLike.map_eq_zero_iff,
215	    QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff]
216	
217	/-- Every class in the kernel of the Čech-units reduction is a truncated-exponential
218	class of an overlap section. -/
219	theorem truncExpClass_surjective :
220	    Function.Surjective (truncExpClass X U₀ U₁) := by
221	  intro y
222	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := (truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv
223	    (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
224	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))).surjective y
225	  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := QuotientAddGroup.mk_surjective q
226	  exact ⟨b, by rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine]; exact hq⟩
227	
228	/-! ## The carrier translation: `range diff` is the additive coboundary subgroup -/
229	
230	/-- **Carrier translation**: the range of the two-cover restriction-difference map
231	`TwoCover.diff` is, as an additive subgroup of the overlap ring, exactly the additive
232	Čech coboundary subgroup `ρ₁(Γ(U₀)) + ρ₂(Γ(U₁))` of the restriction two-chart datum (a
233	difference and a sum of chart sections span the same subgroup). -/
234	theorem range_diff_toAddSubgroup :
235	    (LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)).toAddSubgroup
236	      = cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
237	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) := by
238	  ext b
239	  rw [Submodule.mem_toAddSubgroup, LinearMap.mem_range]
240	  constructor
241	  · rintro ⟨t, rfl⟩
242	    rw [diff_apply]
243	    exact sub_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd _ _ t.1 t.2
244	  · intro hb
245	    obtain ⟨a₁, a₂, ha⟩ := exists_sub_of_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd hb
246	    exact ⟨(a₁, a₂), by rw [diff_apply]; exact ha⟩
247	
248	/-- The two-cover H¹ cokernel `H1Cok`, additively, is the quotient of the overlap ring
249	by the additive Čech coboundaries — the carrier the truncated-exponential engine
250	consumes. Sends `Submodule.Quotient.mk s` to `QuotientAddGroup.mk s`
251	(`h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk`). -/
252	noncomputable def h1CokAddEquivCechQuot :
253	    H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ ≃+
254	      Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
255	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
256	  (submoduleQuotientAddEquiv (LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁))).trans
257	    (QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq (range_diff_toAddSubgroup k X U₀ U₁))
258	
259	@[simp]
260	theorem h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
261	    h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁ (Submodule.Quotient.mk s)
262	      = QuotientAddGroup.mk s :=
263	  rfl
264	
265	/-! ## The keystone: `H¹(X, 𝒪) ≃+ ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) → Ȟ¹ˣ(B))` -/
266	
267	/-- **The truncated-exponential Čech kernel computation of `H¹`** (Kleiman §5
268	Thm 5.11, cocycle leg, carrier form — W5-T2 keystone): for a scheme `X` over `Spec k`
269	and two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf
270	is additively the kernel of the dual-number Čech-units reduction of the cover:
271	
272	```
273	H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)  ≃+  ker( Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)) )
274	```
275	
276	— the two-cover Čech form of `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ ker(Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C))`. Composite of the
277	landed `h1CokEquiv`, the carrier translation `h1CokAddEquivCechQuot`, and the engine
278	`TruncExpCech.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`. On generators: `delta s ↦ truncExpClass s`
279	(`h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta`). Additive only, BY DESIGN — see the module
280	docstring for the `k`-action interface (`mumfordScaling` equivariance). -/
281	noncomputable def h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
282	    (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁) :
283	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃+ Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker :=
284	  (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).toAddEquiv.trans
285	    ((h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁).trans
286	      (truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
287	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))))
288	
289	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁)
290	
291	/-- **Generator formula for the keystone**: the H¹ ↔ ε-kernel identification sends the
292	connecting class `delta s` of an overlap section `s` to the truncated-exponential
293	class `[1 + s ε]`. -/
294	theorem h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
295	    h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
296	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ s := by
297	  have hsplit : h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
298	      (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
299	      = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
300	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))
301	          (h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁
302	            (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))) := rfl
303	  rw [hsplit, h1CokEquiv_delta, h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk, truncExpClass_eq_engine]
304	
305	/-! ## The `k`-action interface (W5-T5): Mumford scaling through the keystone
306	
307	No `SMul k` is placed on the units-kernel side (the D6 distributivity dodge). The
308	`k`-action on `H¹` corresponds pointwise to the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the
309	thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`, acting on truncated-exponential classes by
310	`b ↦ (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a) * b`. -/
311	
312	/-- Scaling a connecting class: the `k`-action on `H¹` hits `delta` as multiplication
313	of the overlap section by the structure constant. -/
314	theorem smul_delta (a : k) (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
315	    a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s
316	      = delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * s) := by
317	  rw [← map_smul]
318	  rfl
319	
320	/-- The keystone on a scaled generator: `a • delta s` goes to the
321	truncated-exponential class of `(X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a) * s`. -/
322	theorem h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_smul_delta (a : k) (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
323	    h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
324	        (a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
325	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * s) := by
326	  rw [smul_delta, h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta]
327	
328	/-- **The Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`** of the two-cover, for
329	a scalar `a : k` (acting through the structure constant
330	`X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a`). Descends to the quotient because the scaling
331	preserves the thickened coboundaries
332	(`TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale`, with the chart compatibility
333	`resHom_overAlgebraMap_left/right`). -/
334	noncomputable def mumfordScaling (a : k) :
335	    ((Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
336	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
337	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) →*
338	      (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
339	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
340	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))) :=
341	  QuotientGroup.map _ _
342	    (Units.map (scaleRingHom (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a)).toMonoidHom)
343	    (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale _ _
344	      (resHom_overAlgebraMap_left k X U₀ U₁ a)
345	      (resHom_overAlgebraMap_right k X U₀ U₁ a))
346	
347	/-- The Mumford scaling acts on truncated-exponential classes by multiplying the
348	overlap section by the structure constant: `[1 + b ε] ↦ [1 + (a·b) ε]`. -/
349	theorem mumfordScaling_mk_truncExpUnit (a : k) (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
350	    mumfordScaling k X U₀ U₁ a (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b))
351	      = QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * b)) :=
352	  unitsScale_mk_truncExpUnit _ _
353	    (resHom_overAlgebraMap_left k X U₀ U₁ a)
354	    (resHom_overAlgebraMap_right k X U₀ U₁ a) b
355	
356	/-- **Mumford-scaling equivariance of the keystone** (the W5 `k`-linearity interface):
357	through `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel`, the honest `k`-action on `H¹(X, 𝒪)`
358	corresponds to the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`. Consumers
359	(W5-T5) run all dimension bookkeeping on the cocycle side — where `k`-linearity is the
360	module structure — and transport pointwise along this lemma; the units-kernel side
361	never carries an `SMul` (the D6 distributivity dodge). Stated on the generators
362	`delta s`; since `delta` is surjective (`delta_surjective`) and both sides are
363	additive in `s`, this determines the correspondence on all of `H¹`. -/
364	theorem mumfordScaling_h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta (a : k)
365	    (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
366	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ (h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
367	        (a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
368	      = mumfordScaling k X U₀ U₁ a
369	          (kerVal X U₀ U₁ (h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
370	            (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))) := by
371	  rw [h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_smul_delta, h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta,
372	    truncExpClass_val, truncExpClass_val]
373	  exact (mumfordScaling_mk_truncExpUnit k X U₀ U₁ a s).symm
374	
375	end TwoCover

9	/-!
10	# `H¹(X, 𝒪) ≃+ ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) → Ȟ¹ˣ(B))` on a two-cover (W5-T2, stage 2)
11	
12	The carrier assembly of the truncated-exponential Čech kernel on the Rebuild's pinned
13	two-cover section rings: for a scheme `X` over `Spec k` with two affine opens
14	`U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, write `B = Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)` for the overlap ring and
15	`ρᵢ = X.resHom : Γ(X, Uᵢ) →+* B` for the restrictions. Composing
16	
17	* the landed two-cover H¹ bridge `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv :
18	  H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`,
19	* the carrier translation `range diff = ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂)` (a difference and a sum of
20	  chart sections span the same additive subgroup — `range_diff_toAddSubgroup`), and
21	* the pure-algebra engine `TruncExpCech.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv :
22	  B ⧸ (ρ₁A₁ + ρ₂A₂) ≃+ Additive (ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)))`
23	
24	gives the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle-leg identification
25	
26	```
27	H¹(X, 𝒪_X)  ≃+  ker( Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)) )
28	```
29	
30	(`TwoCover.h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel`), the two-cover Čech form of
31	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ ker(Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C))`. On generators it sends the connecting class
32	`delta s` of an overlap section to the class of the truncated exponential `1 + s ε`
33	(`h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta`, with the generator map bundled as
34	`TwoCover.truncExpClass`). For the challenge curve, instantiate at an
35	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover` of `C.left` (which exists:
36	`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`); `Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
37	is definitionally the carrier whose `finrank` is `genus C`.
38	
39	**`k`-linearity interface (the D6/R5(iii) distributivity dodge).** The equivalence is
40	additive only, BY DESIGN: no `SMul k` is ever placed on the units-kernel side, so the
41	old draft's unproved `(a+b) • x` Mumford-scaling distributivity is never needed. The
42	`k`-action lives on the H¹/cokernel side, where it is the honest module structure, and
43	corresponds pointwise to the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling (`TwoCover.mumfordScaling`)
44	through the equivalence: `mumfordScaling_h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel`. Dimension
45	counts (W5-T5) should be run on the cocycle side and transported along these pointwise
46	lemmas — never by putting a module structure on the kernel.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `TruncExpCech.submoduleQuotientAddEquiv` — generic bridge: the quotient of a module
51	  by a submodule is, additively, the quotient by the underlying additive subgroup.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.unitsReduction` — the Čech-units reduction
53	  `Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))` of the two-cover.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.truncExpClass` — the kernel class of `1 + b ε` for an
55	  overlap section `b`, with `truncExpClass_add`, `truncExpClass_eq_zero_iff`,
56	  `truncExpClass_surjective`.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel` — the keystone
58	  `H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃+ Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker`, with generator formula
59	  `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.mumfordScaling` + equivariance lemmas — the `k`-action
61	  interface for W5-T5.

65	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, proof of Thm 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020); Mumford,
66	"Abelian varieties", §II.4.
67	-/

78	/-- **The quotient of a module by a submodule is, additively, the quotient by the
79	underlying additive subgroup.** The two quotients have definitionally the same carrier
80	and additive structure (`Submodule.quotientRel` is `QuotientAddGroup.leftRel` of
81	`p.toAddSubgroup` by definition); this packages the identity as an `AddEquiv`, sending
82	`Submodule.Quotient.mk x` to `QuotientAddGroup.mk x`
83	(`submoduleQuotientAddEquiv_mk`). -/
84	def submoduleQuotientAddEquiv {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]
85	    [Module R M] (p : Submodule R M) : (M ⧸ p) ≃+ (M ⧸ p.toAddSubgroup) :=
86	  { Equiv.refl (M ⧸ p) with map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl }
87	
88	@[simp]
89	theorem submoduleQuotientAddEquiv_mk {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [Ring R]
90	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (p : Submodule R M) (x : M) :
91	    submoduleQuotientAddEquiv p (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = QuotientAddGroup.mk x :=
92	  rfl
93	
94	end TruncExpCech

102	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
103	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
104	
105	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
106	
107	/-! ## The two-chart datum of the cover and its compatibility with the constants -/
108	
109	/-- Restriction to the overlap intertwines the structure constants of the two charts:
110	`ρ₁ ∘ (k → Γ(U₀)) = (k → Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))`. -/
111	theorem resHom_overAlgebraMap_left (a : k) :
112	    X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀) (X.overAlgebraMap k U₀ a)
113	      = X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a :=
114	  X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op a
115	
116	/-- Restriction to the overlap intertwines the structure constants of the two charts:
117	`ρ₂ ∘ (k → Γ(U₁)) = (k → Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))`. -/
118	theorem resHom_overAlgebraMap_right (a : k) :
119	    X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁) (X.overAlgebraMap k U₁ a)
120	      = X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a :=
121	  X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op a
122	
123	/-! ## The Čech-units reduction of the two-cover -/
124	
125	/-- **The Čech-units reduction of the two-cover at the dual-number thickening**:
126	`Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁))` for the two-chart datum of restriction ring
127	homomorphisms — the Čech-cocycle incarnation of the restriction
128	`Pic(X ×ₖ Spec k[ε]) → Pic(X)` along `ε ↦ 0`. Reducible wrapper
129	(`unitsReduction_def`) around `TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction`, naming the pinned
130	two-cover instance once (reducible so that all statements below unify transparently
131	with the engine's `cechUnitsReduction` spelling). Its kernel is computed from
132	`H¹(X, 𝒪)` by `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel` below. -/
133	noncomputable abbrev unitsReduction :
134	    ((Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
135	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
136	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) →*
137	      (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁))ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
138	        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
139	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
140	  cechUnitsReduction (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
141	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))
142	
143	/-- `unitsReduction` is `TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction` at the two-cover restriction
144	datum, definitionally. -/
145	theorem unitsReduction_def :
146	    unitsReduction X U₀ U₁
147	      = cechUnitsReduction (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
148	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
149	  rfl
150	
151	/-! ## The truncated-exponential kernel classes of overlap sections -/
152	
153	/-- **The truncated-exponential kernel class of an overlap section**: the class of the
154	unit `1 + b ε` in the kernel of the Čech-units reduction, written additively. This is
155	the generator map of the ε-kernel: `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel` sends the connecting
156	class `delta s` to `truncExpClass s`. -/
157	noncomputable def truncExpClass (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
158	    Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker :=
159	  Additive.ofMul (α := (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker)
160	    ⟨QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b),
161	      MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr
162	        (cechUnitsReduction_mk_truncExpUnit
163	          (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
164	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) b)⟩
165	
166	/-- **The underlying thickened Čech class of an element of the ε-kernel** — the
167	coercion `Additive (ker) → Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])` as a named map. Kernel discipline: one
168	opaque head for the coercion seam, so that rewriting under it never re-elaborates the
169	scheme-tower coercions (`kerVal_eq_coe` recovers the raw coercion). -/
170	noncomputable def kerVal (y : Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
171	    (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
172	      (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
173	      (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))) :=
174	  (Additive.toMul y : (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker).1
175	
176	/-- `kerVal` is the raw coercion, definitionally. -/
177	theorem kerVal_eq_coe (y : Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
178	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ y
179	      = ((Additive.toMul y : (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker) :
180	          (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
181	            (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
182	            (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) :=
183	  rfl
184	
185	/-- The underlying thickened Čech class of `truncExpClass b` is `[1 + b ε]`.
186	Definitional. -/
187	theorem truncExpClass_val (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
188	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ (truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b) = QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :=
189	  rfl
190	
191	/-- `truncExpClass` is the truncated-exponential kernel engine applied to the residue
192	class of the section: `truncExpClass b = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv ρ₁ ρ₂ [b]`.
193	Definitional; the workhorse normal form for the lemmas below. -/
194	theorem truncExpClass_eq_engine (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
195	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b
196	      = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
197	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) (QuotientAddGroup.mk b) :=
198	  rfl
199	
200	/-- Additivity of the truncated-exponential kernel classes:
201	`(1 + bε)(1 + cε) = 1 + (b+c)ε`. -/
202	theorem truncExpClass_add (b c : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
203	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ (b + c)
204	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b + truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ c := by
205	  rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine X U₀ U₁ b, truncExpClass_eq_engine X U₀ U₁ c, ← map_add,
206	    ← QuotientAddGroup.mk_add, ← truncExpClass_eq_engine]
207	
208	/-- Vanishing of a truncated-exponential kernel class: `[1 + b ε] = 0` iff `b` is a
209	Čech coboundary `ρ₁ a₁ + ρ₂ a₂` of the two charts. -/
210	theorem truncExpClass_eq_zero_iff (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
211	    truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ b = 0
212	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
213	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) := by
214	  rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine, EmbeddingLike.map_eq_zero_iff,
215	    QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff]
216	
217	/-- Every class in the kernel of the Čech-units reduction is a truncated-exponential
218	class of an overlap section. -/
219	theorem truncExpClass_surjective :
220	    Function.Surjective (truncExpClass X U₀ U₁) := by
221	  intro y
222	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := (truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv
223	    (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
224	    (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))).surjective y
225	  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := QuotientAddGroup.mk_surjective q
226	  exact ⟨b, by rw [truncExpClass_eq_engine]; exact hq⟩
227	
228	/-! ## The carrier translation: `range diff` is the additive coboundary subgroup -/
229	
230	/-- **Carrier translation**: the range of the two-cover restriction-difference map
231	`TwoCover.diff` is, as an additive subgroup of the overlap ring, exactly the additive
232	Čech coboundary subgroup `ρ₁(Γ(U₀)) + ρ₂(Γ(U₁))` of the restriction two-chart datum (a
233	difference and a sum of chart sections span the same subgroup). -/
234	theorem range_diff_toAddSubgroup :
235	    (LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)).toAddSubgroup
236	      = cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
237	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) := by
238	  ext b
239	  rw [Submodule.mem_toAddSubgroup, LinearMap.mem_range]
240	  constructor
241	  · rintro ⟨t, rfl⟩
242	    rw [diff_apply]
243	    exact sub_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd _ _ t.1 t.2
244	  · intro hb
245	    obtain ⟨a₁, a₂, ha⟩ := exists_sub_of_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd hb
246	    exact ⟨(a₁, a₂), by rw [diff_apply]; exact ha⟩
247	
248	/-- The two-cover H¹ cokernel `H1Cok`, additively, is the quotient of the overlap ring
249	by the additive Čech coboundaries — the carrier the truncated-exponential engine
250	consumes. Sends `Submodule.Quotient.mk s` to `QuotientAddGroup.mk s`
251	(`h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk`). -/
252	noncomputable def h1CokAddEquivCechQuot :
253	    H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ ≃+
254	      Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ cechCoboundaryAdd (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
255	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)) :=
256	  (submoduleQuotientAddEquiv (LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁))).trans
257	    (QuotientAddGroup.quotientAddEquivOfEq (range_diff_toAddSubgroup k X U₀ U₁))
258	
259	@[simp]
260	theorem h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
261	    h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁ (Submodule.Quotient.mk s)
262	      = QuotientAddGroup.mk s :=
263	  rfl
264	
265	/-! ## The keystone: `H¹(X, 𝒪) ≃+ ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) → Ȟ¹ˣ(B))` -/
266	
267	/-- **The truncated-exponential Čech kernel computation of `H¹`** (Kleiman §5
268	Thm 5.11, cocycle leg, carrier form — W5-T2 keystone): for a scheme `X` over `Spec k`
269	and two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf
270	is additively the kernel of the dual-number Čech-units reduction of the cover:
271	
272	```
273	H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)  ≃+  ker( Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)) )
274	```
275	
276	— the two-cover Čech form of `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ ker(Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C))`. Composite of the
277	landed `h1CokEquiv`, the carrier translation `h1CokAddEquivCechQuot`, and the engine
278	`TruncExpCech.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`. On generators: `delta s ↦ truncExpClass s`
279	(`h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta`). Additive only, BY DESIGN — see the module
280	docstring for the `k`-action interface (`mumfordScaling` equivariance). -/
281	noncomputable def h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
282	    (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁) :
283	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃+ Additive (unitsReduction X U₀ U₁).ker :=
284	  (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).toAddEquiv.trans
285	    ((h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁).trans
286	      (truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
287	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))))
288	
289	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁)
290	
291	/-- **Generator formula for the keystone**: the H¹ ↔ ε-kernel identification sends the
292	connecting class `delta s` of an overlap section `s` to the truncated-exponential
293	class `[1 + s ε]`. -/
294	theorem h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
295	    h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
296	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ s := by
297	  have hsplit : h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
298	      (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
299	      = truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀))
300	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))
301	          (h1CokAddEquivCechQuot k X U₀ U₁
302	            (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))) := rfl
303	  rw [hsplit, h1CokEquiv_delta, h1CokAddEquivCechQuot_mk, truncExpClass_eq_engine]
304	
305	/-! ## The `k`-action interface (W5-T5): Mumford scaling through the keystone
306	
307	No `SMul k` is placed on the units-kernel side (the D6 distributivity dodge). The
308	`k`-action on `H¹` corresponds pointwise to the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the
309	thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`, acting on truncated-exponential classes by
310	`b ↦ (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a) * b`. -/
311	
312	/-- Scaling a connecting class: the `k`-action on `H¹` hits `delta` as multiplication
313	of the overlap section by the structure constant. -/
314	theorem smul_delta (a : k) (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
315	    a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s
316	      = delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * s) := by
317	  rw [← map_smul]
318	  rfl
319	
320	/-- The keystone on a scaled generator: `a • delta s` goes to the
321	truncated-exponential class of `(X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a) * s`. -/
322	theorem h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_smul_delta (a : k) (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
323	    h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
324	        (a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s)
325	      = truncExpClass X U₀ U₁ (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * s) := by
326	  rw [smul_delta, h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta]
327	
328	/-- **The Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`** of the two-cover, for
329	a scalar `a : k` (acting through the structure constant
330	`X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a`). Descends to the quotient because the scaling
331	preserves the thickened coboundaries
332	(`TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale`, with the chart compatibility
333	`resHom_overAlgebraMap_left/right`). -/
334	noncomputable def mumfordScaling (a : k) :
335	    ((Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
336	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
337	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)))) →*
338	      (Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
339	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)))
340	        (mapRingHom (X.resHom (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁))) :=
341	  QuotientGroup.map _ _
342	    (Units.map (scaleRingHom (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a)).toMonoidHom)
343	    (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale _ _
344	      (resHom_overAlgebraMap_left k X U₀ U₁ a)
345	      (resHom_overAlgebraMap_right k X U₀ U₁ a))
346	
347	/-- The Mumford scaling acts on truncated-exponential classes by multiplying the
348	overlap section by the structure constant: `[1 + b ε] ↦ [1 + (a·b) ε]`. -/
349	theorem mumfordScaling_mk_truncExpUnit (a : k) (b : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
350	    mumfordScaling k X U₀ U₁ a (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b))
351	      = QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit (X.overAlgebraMap k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) a * b)) :=
352	  unitsScale_mk_truncExpUnit _ _
353	    (resHom_overAlgebraMap_left k X U₀ U₁ a)
354	    (resHom_overAlgebraMap_right k X U₀ U₁ a) b
355	
356	/-- **Mumford-scaling equivariance of the keystone** (the W5 `k`-linearity interface):
357	through `h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel`, the honest `k`-action on `H¹(X, 𝒪)`
358	corresponds to the Mumford `ε ↦ aε` scaling of the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`. Consumers
359	(W5-T5) run all dimension bookkeeping on the cocycle side — where `k`-linearity is the
360	module structure — and transport pointwise along this lemma; the units-kernel side
361	never carries an `SMul` (the D6 distributivity dodge). Stated on the generators
362	`delta s`; since `delta` is surjective (`delta_surjective`) and both sides are
363	additive in `s`, this determines the correspondence on all of `H¹`. -/
364	theorem mumfordScaling_h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta (a : k)
365	    (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
366	    kerVal X U₀ U₁ (h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
367	        (a • delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
368	      = mumfordScaling k X U₀ U₁ a
369	          (kerVal X U₀ U₁ (h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁
370	            (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))) := by
371	  rw [h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_smul_delta, h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel_delta,
372	    truncExpClass_val, truncExpClass_val]
373	  exact (mumfordScaling_mk_truncExpUnit k X U₀ U₁ a s).symm
374	
375	end TwoCover

8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
67	-/

8	/-!
9	# The two-chart Čech unit-cocycle engine (W5-T2, algebra layer)
10	
11	The pure-algebra heart of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle leg. A *two-chart datum* is a
12	pair of ring homomorphisms `ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B`, `ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B` — think `Aᵢ = Γ(Uᵢ, 𝒪_C)`
13	the section rings of a 2-affine cover and `B = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, 𝒪_C)` the overlap ring, with
14	`ρᵢ` the restrictions. The two-cover Čech `Ȟ¹` of *units* is the quotient
15	`Bˣ ⧸ (im ρ₁ˣ · im ρ₂ˣ)` of transition units by coboundaries — the Picard group of the
16	cover in Čech form. Applying the same construction to the dual-number thickening
17	(`Aᵢ[ε] →+* B[ε]` via `TruncExpCech.mapRingHom`) and reducing mod `ε` (`unitsFst`, which
18	maps coboundaries to coboundaries) gives the restriction map `Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)` of
19	`Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C)`.
20	
21	The engine computes the **kernel** of that reduction: the truncated exponential
22	`b ↦ [1 + b ε]` induces an additive equivalence
23	
24	```
25	B ⧸ (ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂))  ≃+  ker(Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) → Ȟ¹ˣ(B))
26	```
27	
28	(`truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`), whose source is exactly the two-chart Čech cokernel
29	shape of `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok` (`Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`) — i.e.
30	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` on a curve; the carrier assembly is
31	`AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TruncExpCechH1`. Equivariance for the Mumford `ε ↦ tε`
32	scaling (`scaleRingHom`) is provided pointwise: `unitsScale_mk_truncExpUnit` shows the
33	scaling acts on truncated-exponential classes as `b ↦ t·b`, matching the `k`-scalar
34	action on `H1Cok`.
35	
36	**Design note (the `(a+b)•x` distributivity trap, worksheet D6 / recon R5(iii))**: no
37	`SMul`/`Module` structure is ever placed on the units-kernel side. All `k`-linearity
38	bookkeeping stays on the Čech-cokernel side `B ⧸ (ρ₁A₁ + ρ₂A₂)`, where it is the honest
39	module structure of a quotient of section modules; the Mumford scaling is related to it
40	only through the pointwise equivariance lemmas above. In particular the old draft's
41	unproved scalar distributivity for the functorial scaling action is *dodged*, not
42	needed.
43	
44	Everything here is elementary commutative algebra: no schemes, no sheaves. Ported
45	(Wave-5 brick T2, stage 1) from the old draft's
46	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6,
47	re-proved against the Rebuild's pin, in the collision-safe project namespace
48	`TruncExpCech` (see `AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TruncExpUnits`).
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂ : Subgroup Bˣ` — the coboundary subgroup
53	  `im(ρ₁ˣ) · im(ρ₂ˣ)`, so `Bˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits` is the two-cover Čech `Ȟ¹` of
54	  units.
55	* `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ : AddSubgroup B` — the additive coboundaries
56	  `ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂)`.
57	* `TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂ : Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)` — reduction mod `ε`.
58	* `TruncExpCech.truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv :
59	  B ⧸ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ ≃+ Additive (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker` — the
60	  keystone kernel computation.
61	* `TruncExpCech.unitsScale_mk_truncExpUnit`,
62	  `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale` — Mumford-scaling
63	  equivariance.
64	
65	## References
66	
67	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, proof of Thm 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020); Mumford,
68	"Abelian varieties", §II.4.
69	-/

72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

74	universe u v w
75	
76	namespace TruncExpCech
77	
78	open TrivSqZeroExt DualNumber
79	
80	variable {A₁ : Type u} {A₂ : Type v} {B : Type w}
81	variable [CommRing A₁] [CommRing A₂] [CommRing B]
82	
83	/-! ## The coboundary subgroups of a two-chart datum -/
84	
85	/-- **The Čech coboundary subgroup of a two-chart datum**: for restriction
86	homomorphisms `ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B`, `ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B` onto the overlap ring `B`, the subgroup
87	`im(ρ₁ˣ) · im(ρ₂ˣ) ≤ Bˣ` of transition units that are coboundaries of the 2-cover. The
88	quotient `Bˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂` is the two-cover Čech `Ȟ¹` of units — the
89	Čech-cocycle Picard group of the cover. -/
90	def cechCoboundaryUnits (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) : Subgroup Bˣ :=
91	  (Units.map ρ₁.toMonoidHom).range ⊔ (Units.map ρ₂.toMonoidHom).range
92	
93	/-- Membership in the Čech coboundary subgroup: `u` is a coboundary iff
94	`u = ρ₁ˣ(v₁) · ρ₂ˣ(v₂)` for chart units `vᵢ ∈ Aᵢˣ` (the sign convention with a product
95	rather than a quotient is immaterial: the ranges are subgroups). -/
96	theorem mem_cechCoboundaryUnits {ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B} {ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B} {u : Bˣ} :
97	    u ∈ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂
98	      ↔ ∃ (v₁ : A₁ˣ) (v₂ : A₂ˣ),
99	          Units.map ρ₁.toMonoidHom v₁ * Units.map ρ₂.toMonoidHom v₂ = u := by
100	  constructor
101	  · intro h
102	    obtain ⟨y, hy, z, hz, rfl⟩ := Subgroup.mem_sup.mp h
103	    obtain ⟨v₁, rfl⟩ := MonoidHom.mem_range.mp hy
104	    obtain ⟨v₂, rfl⟩ := MonoidHom.mem_range.mp hz
105	    exact ⟨v₁, v₂, rfl⟩
106	  · rintro ⟨v₁, v₂, rfl⟩
107	    exact Subgroup.mem_sup.mpr
108	      ⟨_, MonoidHom.mem_range.mpr ⟨v₁, rfl⟩, _, MonoidHom.mem_range.mpr ⟨v₂, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
109	
110	/-- Chart units from the first chart are coboundaries. -/
111	theorem unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
112	    (v : A₁ˣ) : Units.map ρ₁.toMonoidHom v ∈ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂ :=
113	  mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr ⟨v, 1, by simp⟩
114	
115	/-- Chart units from the second chart are coboundaries. -/
116	theorem unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_right (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
117	    (v : A₂ˣ) : Units.map ρ₂.toMonoidHom v ∈ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂ :=
118	  mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr ⟨1, v, by simp⟩
119	
120	/-- **The additive Čech coboundary subgroup of a two-chart datum**:
121	`ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂) ≤ B` as an additive subgroup. The quotient
122	`B ⧸ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂` is the two-cover Čech cokernel — for the section rings of
123	a 2-affine cover, exactly the carrier shape of `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`
124	(`Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`; a difference `ρ₁ a₁ - ρ₂ a₂` and a sum `ρ₁ a₁ + ρ₂ a₂` span
125	the same subgroup). -/
126	def cechCoboundaryAdd (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) : AddSubgroup B :=
127	  ρ₁.toAddMonoidHom.range ⊔ ρ₂.toAddMonoidHom.range
128	
129	/-- Membership in the additive Čech coboundary subgroup. -/
130	theorem mem_cechCoboundaryAdd {ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B} {ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B} {b : B} :
131	    b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ ↔ ∃ (a₁ : A₁) (a₂ : A₂), ρ₁ a₁ + ρ₂ a₂ = b := by
132	  constructor
133	  · intro h
134	    obtain ⟨y, hy, z, hz, rfl⟩ := AddSubgroup.mem_sup.mp h
135	    obtain ⟨a₁, rfl⟩ := AddMonoidHom.mem_range.mp hy
136	    obtain ⟨a₂, rfl⟩ := AddMonoidHom.mem_range.mp hz
137	    exact ⟨a₁, a₂, rfl⟩
138	  · rintro ⟨a₁, a₂, rfl⟩
139	    exact AddSubgroup.mem_sup.mpr
140	      ⟨_, AddMonoidHom.mem_range.mpr ⟨a₁, rfl⟩, _, AddMonoidHom.mem_range.mpr ⟨a₂, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
141	
142	/-- Differences of chart sections are additive Čech coboundaries — the subtraction form
143	of membership, matching the difference-of-restrictions map
144	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.diff` of the geometric consumer. Clean-binder helper: state
145	and use this on abstract rings, then transport the result along the (defeq) carrier
146	identifications of the sheaf dialect. -/
147	theorem sub_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
148	    (a₁ : A₁) (a₂ : A₂) :
149	    ρ₁ a₁ - ρ₂ a₂ ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ :=
150	  mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mpr ⟨a₁, -a₂, by rw [map_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg]⟩
151	
152	/-- Additive Čech coboundaries are differences of chart sections — the subtraction form
153	of the membership characterisation (converse of `sub_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd`). -/
154	theorem exists_sub_of_mem_cechCoboundaryAdd {ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B} {ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B}
155	    {b : B} (h : b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂) :
156	    ∃ (a₁ : A₁) (a₂ : A₂), ρ₁ a₁ - ρ₂ a₂ = b := by
157	  obtain ⟨a₁, a₂, ha⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mp h
158	  exact ⟨a₁, -a₂, by rw [map_neg, sub_neg_eq_add, ha]⟩
159	
160	/-! ## The truncated exponential detects the additive coboundaries -/
161	
162	/-- **The truncated exponential detects the additive coboundaries** (the
163	well-definedness/injectivity heart of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle leg): the unit
164	`1 + b ε` on the dual-number overlap ring is a coboundary of the thickened cover iff
165	`b` is an additive coboundary `ρ₁(a₁) + ρ₂(a₂)`.
166	
167	Forward direction: decompose the two chart units `wᵢ ∈ (Aᵢ[ε])ˣ` as
168	`inl(wᵢ₀)·(1 + cᵢ ε)` (`unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit`); reducing the coboundary
169	relation mod `ε` forces the constant parts to cancel, leaving
170	`1 + b ε = 1 + (ρ₁ c₁ + ρ₂ c₂) ε`. -/
171	theorem truncExpUnit_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_iff
172	    (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) (b : B) :
173	    truncExpUnit b ∈ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
174	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ := by
175	  constructor
176	  · intro h
177	    obtain ⟨w₁, w₂, hw⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp h
178	    rw [← unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit w₁,
179	      ← unitsInl_unitsFst_mul_truncExpUnit w₂, map_mul, map_mul,
180	      unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl, unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl,
181	      map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit,
182	      mul_mul_mul_comm, ← map_mul, ← truncExpUnit_add] at hw
183	    -- reduce mod `ε`: the constant part of the coboundary is trivial
184	    have hfst := congrArg unitsFst hw
185	    rw [map_mul, unitsFst_unitsInl, unitsFst_truncExpUnit, mul_one,
186	      unitsFst_truncExpUnit] at hfst
187	    rw [hfst, map_one, one_mul] at hw
188	    exact mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mpr ⟨_, _, truncExpUnit_injective hw⟩
189	  · intro h
190	    obtain ⟨a₁, a₂, rfl⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryAdd.mp h
191	    refine mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr ⟨truncExpUnit a₁, truncExpUnit a₂, ?_⟩
192	    rw [map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, map_mapRingHom_truncExpUnit, ← truncExpUnit_add]
193	
194	/-! ## The Čech reduction map and its kernel -/
195	
196	/-- Reduction mod `ε` on units carries thickened coboundaries to coboundaries
197	(`unitsFst` naturality), so it descends to the Čech `Ȟ¹` quotients. -/
198	theorem cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsFst (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
199	    cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂) ≤
200	      (cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂).comap (unitsFst (R := B)) := by
201	  intro u hu
202	  obtain ⟨w₁, w₂, rfl⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
203	  refine Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr
204	    ⟨unitsFst w₁, unitsFst w₂, ?_⟩)
205	  rw [map_mul, unitsFst_map_mapRingHom, unitsFst_map_mapRingHom]
206	
207	/-- **The reduction map of two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`-of-units groups**
208	`Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B)` induced by reduction mod `ε` — the Čech-cocycle incarnation of
209	the restriction `Pic(C ×_k Spec k[ε]) → Pic(C)` along `ε ↦ 0`. Its kernel is computed
210	by `truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv` below. -/
211	noncomputable def cechUnitsReduction (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
212	    ((B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) →*
213	      Bˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits ρ₁ ρ₂ :=
214	  QuotientGroup.map _ _ (unitsFst (R := B))
215	    (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsFst ρ₁ ρ₂)
216	
217	/-- Truncated-exponential classes lie in the kernel of the Čech reduction map:
218	`1 + b ε` reduces to `1` mod `ε`. -/
219	theorem cechUnitsReduction_mk_truncExpUnit (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
220	    (b : B) :
221	    cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂ (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b)) = 1 := by
222	  rw [cechUnitsReduction, QuotientGroup.map_mk, unitsFst_truncExpUnit,
223	    QuotientGroup.mk_one]
224	
225	/-- Vanishing of a truncated-exponential class in the thickened Čech `Ȟ¹`:
226	`[1 + b ε] = 1` iff `b` is an additive coboundary. -/
227	theorem mk_truncExpUnit_eq_one_iff (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) (b : B) :
228	    (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
229	        (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) = 1
230	      ↔ b ∈ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ := by
231	  rw [QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
232	  exact truncExpUnit_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_iff ρ₁ ρ₂ b
233	
234	/-- **Every kernel class of the Čech reduction is a truncated exponential** (the
235	surjectivity heart of the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11 cocycle leg): a class of `Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε])`
236	restricting trivially mod `ε` is represented by `1 + b ε` for some `b : B`. Proof:
237	normalise a representative `u` by the (lifted) chart units trivialising its reduction;
238	the corrected unit has trivial constant part, hence lies in the range of the truncated
239	exponential (`truncExp_range_eq_ker_unitsFst`). -/
240	theorem exists_mk_truncExpUnit_of_cechUnitsReduction_eq_one
241	    (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
242	    (x : (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂))
243	    (hx : cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂ x = 1) :
244	    ∃ b : B, (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
245	      (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) = x := by
246	  revert hx
247	  induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
248	  | H u =>
249	    intro hu
250	    rw [cechUnitsReduction, QuotientGroup.map_mk, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] at hu
251	    obtain ⟨v₁, v₂, hv⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
252	    -- the chart-unit correction of `u`
253	    have hker : unitsFst
254	        ((Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₁).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₁))⁻¹ * u *
255	          (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₂).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₂))⁻¹) = 1 := by
256	      rw [map_mul, map_mul, map_inv, map_inv, unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl,
257	        unitsMap_mapRingHom_unitsInl, unitsFst_unitsInl, unitsFst_unitsInl, ← hv]
258	      group
259	    have hmem : (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₁).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₁))⁻¹ * u *
260	        (Units.map (mapRingHom ρ₂).toMonoidHom (unitsInl v₂))⁻¹
261	          ∈ (truncExp (R := B)).range := by
262	      rw [truncExp_range_eq_ker_unitsFst]
263	      exact MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr hker
264	    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := MonoidHom.mem_range.mp hmem
265	    refine ⟨m.toAdd, ?_⟩
266	    rw [← truncExp_apply, hm, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_mul,
267	      QuotientGroup.mk_inv, QuotientGroup.mk_inv,
268	      (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr
269	        (unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
270	          (unitsInl v₁)),
271	      (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr
272	        (unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_right (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)
273	          (unitsInl v₂))]
274	    simp

276	/-! ## The kernel computation -/
277	
278	/-- The truncated exponential as a monoid homomorphism into the kernel of the Čech
279	reduction map (multiplicative source `Multiplicative B`). -/
280	noncomputable def truncExpCechKernelMonoidHom (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
281	    Multiplicative B →* (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker where
282	  toFun b :=
283	    ⟨QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b.toAdd),
284	      MonoidHom.mem_ker.mpr (cechUnitsReduction_mk_truncExpUnit ρ₁ ρ₂ b.toAdd)⟩
285	  map_one' := Subtype.ext <| by
286	    change (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit ((1 : Multiplicative B).toAdd)) : _) = 1
287	    rw [toAdd_one, truncExpUnit_zero, QuotientGroup.mk_one]
288	  map_mul' b c := Subtype.ext <| by
289	    change (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit ((b * c).toAdd)) : _) = _
290	    rw [toAdd_mul, truncExpUnit_add, QuotientGroup.mk_mul]
291	    rfl
292	
293	/-- **The truncated-exponential kernel computation** (Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11, cocycle leg,
294	algebra layer): for a two-chart datum `ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B`, `ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B`, the truncated
295	exponential `b ↦ [1 + b ε]` induces an additive equivalence
296	
297	```
298	B ⧸ (ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂))  ≃+  ker( Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε]) →* Ȟ¹ˣ(B) )
299	```
300	
301	from the two-cover Čech cokernel (the `AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok` carrier
302	shape — `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` for the section rings of a 2-affine cover of a curve) onto the
303	kernel of the dual-number Čech-units reduction (the two-chart
304	`ker(Pic(C_ε) → Pic(C))`). Well-definedness and injectivity are
305	`mk_truncExpUnit_eq_one_iff`; surjectivity is
306	`exists_mk_truncExpUnit_of_cechUnitsReduction_eq_one`; additivity is the
307	truncated-exponential functional equation `truncExpUnit_add`. -/
308	noncomputable def truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B) :
309	    B ⧸ cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂ ≃+
310	      Additive (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker := by
311	  refine AddEquiv.ofBijective
312	    (QuotientAddGroup.lift (cechCoboundaryAdd ρ₁ ρ₂)
313	      (MonoidHom.toAdditiveRight (truncExpCechKernelMonoidHom ρ₁ ρ₂)) ?_) ⟨?_, ?_⟩
314	  · intro b hb
315	    apply Additive.toMul.injective
316	    apply Subtype.ext
317	    change (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) : _) = 1
318	    exact (mk_truncExpUnit_eq_one_iff ρ₁ ρ₂ b).mpr hb
319	  · rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
320	    intro x
321	    induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on with
322	    | H b =>
323	      intro hbx
324	      have hb : (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
325	          (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) = 1 :=
326	        congrArg (fun y => (Additive.toMul y : (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker).1) hbx
327	      rw [QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff]
328	      exact (mk_truncExpUnit_eq_one_iff ρ₁ ρ₂ b).mp hb
329	  · intro y
330	    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := exists_mk_truncExpUnit_of_cechUnitsReduction_eq_one ρ₁ ρ₂
331	      (Additive.toMul y : (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker).1
332	      (Additive.toMul y : (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker).2
333	    exact ⟨QuotientAddGroup.mk b,
334	      Additive.toMul.injective (Subtype.ext hb)⟩
335	
336	/-- Elementwise formula for the truncated-exponential kernel equivalence on residue
337	classes: `[b] ↦ [1 + b ε]`. Definitional. -/
338	theorem truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv_apply_mk (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
339	    (b : B) :
340	    ((Additive.toMul (truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv ρ₁ ρ₂ (QuotientAddGroup.mk b)) :
341	        (cechUnitsReduction ρ₁ ρ₂).ker) : _)
342	      = (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b) :
343	          (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) :=
344	  rfl
345	
346	/-! ## Mumford-scaling equivariance of the engine
347	
348	The `ε ↦ tε` scaling of the overlap ring `B[ε]` (`scaleRingHom t`) preserves the
349	thickened coboundaries whenever the scalar is compatible with the charts
350	(`ρ₁ s₁ = t = ρ₂ s₂` — for a `k`-algebra datum, `sᵢ` and `t` are the images of a common
351	`a ∈ k`), hence descends to `Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε])`, and it acts on truncated-exponential classes
352	exactly by `b ↦ t·b` — matching the `k`-scalar action on the Čech cokernel side of
353	`truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`. -/
354	
355	/-- The `ε ↦ tε` scaling preserves the thickened Čech coboundaries when the scalar `t`
356	is compatible with the charts (`ρ₁ s₁ = t = ρ₂ s₂`). -/
357	theorem cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
358	    {s₁ : A₁} {s₂ : A₂} {t : B} (h₁ : ρ₁ s₁ = t) (h₂ : ρ₂ s₂ = t) :
359	    cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂) ≤
360	      (cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)).comap
361	        (Units.map (scaleRingHom t).toMonoidHom) := by
362	  intro u hu
363	  obtain ⟨w₁, w₂, rfl⟩ := mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
364	  refine Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr
365	    ⟨Units.map (scaleRingHom s₁).toMonoidHom w₁,
366	     Units.map (scaleRingHom s₂).toMonoidHom w₂, ?_⟩)
367	  rw [map_mul]
368	  congr 1
369	  · apply Units.ext
370	    simp only [Units.coe_map]
371	    exact (RingHom.congr_fun (mapRingHom_comp_scaleRingHom ρ₁ s₁) (w₁ : A₁[ε])).trans
372	      (by rw [h₁]; rfl)
373	  · apply Units.ext
374	    simp only [Units.coe_map]
375	    exact (RingHom.congr_fun (mapRingHom_comp_scaleRingHom ρ₂ s₂) (w₂ : A₂[ε])).trans
376	      (by rw [h₂]; rfl)
377	
378	/-- **Equivariance of the truncated-exponential classes under the Mumford scaling**:
379	the `ε ↦ tε` scaling of `Ȟ¹ˣ(B[ε])` carries `[1 + b ε]` to `[1 + (t·b) ε]` — through
380	`truncExpCechKernelAddEquiv`, the scaling acts on the Čech cokernel
381	`B ⧸ (ρ₁(A₁) + ρ₂(A₂))` as multiplication by `t`, i.e. as the `k`-scalar action for a
382	`k`-algebra two-chart datum. -/
383	theorem unitsScale_mk_truncExpUnit (ρ₁ : A₁ →+* B) (ρ₂ : A₂ →+* B)
384	    {s₁ : A₁} {s₂ : A₂} {t : B} (h₁ : ρ₁ s₁ = t) (h₂ : ρ₂ s₂ = t) (b : B) :
385	    QuotientGroup.map _ _ (Units.map (scaleRingHom t).toMonoidHom)
386	        (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsScale ρ₁ ρ₂ h₁ h₂)
387	        (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit b))
388	      = (QuotientGroup.mk (truncExpUnit (t * b)) :
389	          (B[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom ρ₁) (mapRingHom ρ₂)) := by
390	  rw [QuotientGroup.map_mk, unitsScale_truncExpUnit]
391	
392	end TruncExpCech

9	/-!
10	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
11	
12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
13	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
14	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
15	modules:
16	
17	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
18	
19	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
20	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
21	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
22	function spaces.
23	
24	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
25	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
26	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
27	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
28	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
29	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
34	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
35	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
36	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
37	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
38	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
39	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
40	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
41	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
42	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
43	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
44	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
45	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
46	
47	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
48	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
49	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
50	-/

64	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

66	/-- The Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the small Zariski site of a
67	scheme `X`, for two opens covering `X`. -/
68	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverSquare (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
69	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)).MayerVietorisSquare :=
70	  Opens.mayerVietorisSquare'
71	    { X₁ := U₀ ⊓ U₁
72	      X₂ := U₀
73	      X₃ := U₁
74	      X₄ := ⊤
75	      f₁₂ := homOfLE inf_le_left
76	      f₁₃ := homOfLE inf_le_right
77	      f₂₄ := homOfLE le_top
78	      f₃₄ := homOfLE le_top
79	      fac := Subsingleton.elim _ _ } hcov.symm rfl
80	
81	end Square

83	section GeneralCoefficients
84	
85	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
86	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
87	
88	/-- **The two-cover H¹ computation, general coefficients.** For a sheaf `F` of
89	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`, two opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` and
90	vanishing `H¹'(U₀, F)`, `H¹'(U₁, F)`, the degree-one cohomology of the site is the
91	cokernel of the restriction-difference map `F(U₀) × F(U₁) → F(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`. -/
92	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv
93	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
94	    (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
95	    [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1)] [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1)] :
96	    Sheaf.HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k]
97	      (F.obj.obj (op (U₀ ⊓ U₁)) ⧸
98	        LinearMap.range ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff F)) :=
99	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
100	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1))
101	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
102	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1))
103	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) F 1).trans
104	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv F).symm
105	
106	end GeneralCoefficients

108	namespace TwoCover
109	
110	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
111	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
112	
113	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
114	
115	/-- The restriction-difference map `Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`,
116	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁} - s₁|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁}` (see `TwoCover.diff_apply`), with the
117	`k`-module structures of `Scheme.overModule`. -/
118	noncomputable def diff : (Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
119	  ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom.comp
120	      (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
121	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom.comp
122	      (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
123	
124	lemma diff_apply (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
125	    diff k X U₀ U₁ t = X.resHom inf_le_left t.1 - X.resHom inf_le_right t.2 :=
126	  rfl
127	
128	/-- The two-cover difference map is the Mayer–Vietoris restriction-difference map of the
129	associated square. -/
130	lemma diff_eq_moduleDiff (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
131	    diff k X U₀ U₁ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) :=
132	  rfl
133	
134	/-- **The two-cover H¹ cokernel carrier**: the cokernel of the restriction-difference
135	map, `Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range (TwoCover.diff)`. For `U₀, U₁` an affine open cover this is
136	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)` (see `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`); it is a plain quotient of section modules, so
137	`Module.finrank` arguments can be run on it directly. -/
138	noncomputable abbrev H1Cok : Type u :=
139	  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)
140	
141	/-- A section extending to `U₀` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
142	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
143	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_left t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
144	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
145	  exact ⟨(t, 0), by rw [diff_apply]; simp⟩
146	
147	/-- A section extending to `U₁` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
148	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
149	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_right t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
150	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
151	  refine ⟨(0, -t), ?_⟩
152	  rw [diff_apply]
153	  simp
