155	section Bridge
156	
157	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
158	
159	/-- The two-cover connecting map: the degree-one cohomology class of a section on the
160	overlap `U₀ ⊓ U₁`, in the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule` of the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
161	noncomputable def delta :
162	    Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 :=
163	  ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
164	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm.toLinearMap).comp
165	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k))
166	
167	/-- The connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes. -/
168	lemma delta_diff (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
169	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 := by
170	  have h : (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
171	      (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 :=
172	    (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) t
173	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) =
174	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
175	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
176	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
177	          (diff k X U₀ U₁ t)) from rfl, h]
178	  exact map_zero _
179	
180	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₀` vanishes. -/
181	lemma delta_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
182	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_left t) = 0 := by
183	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_left t = diff k X U₀ U₁ (t, 0) := by
184	    rw [diff_apply]
185	    simp
186	  rw [h, delta_diff]
187	
188	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₁` vanishes. -/
189	lemma delta_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
190	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_right t) = 0 := by
191	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_right t = -diff k X U₀ U₁ (0, t) := by
192	    rw [diff_apply]
193	    simp
194	  rw [h, map_neg, delta_diff, neg_zero]
195	
196	variable (hU₀ : IsAffineOpen U₀) (hU₁ : IsAffineOpen U₁)
197	
198	include hU₀ hU₁ in
199	/-- For an affine two-cover, the connecting map is surjective: every degree-one class
200	comes from a section on the overlap. -/
201	lemma delta_surjective : Function.Surjective (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov) := by
202	  haveI : Subsingleton
203	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
204	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
205	  haveI : Subsingleton
206	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
207	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
208	  intro y
209	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_surjective (X.moduleKSheaf k)
210	    ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
211	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1) y)
212	  refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
213	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s =
214	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
215	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
216	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s) from rfl, hs,
217	    LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
218	
219	/-- **The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge.** For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and two
220	affine opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf as a
221	sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X` is the cokernel of the
222	restriction-difference map on sections:
223	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|∩ - s₁|∩)`.
224	The inverse sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class
225	(`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv_delta`). -/
226	noncomputable def h1CokEquiv :
227	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ :=
228	  letI : Subsingleton
229	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
230	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
231	  letI : Subsingleton
232	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
233	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
234	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
235	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).trans
236	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
237	
238	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map: the bridge sends the connecting
239	class of a section on the overlap to its class in the cokernel. -/
240	lemma h1CokEquiv_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
241	    h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s) =
242	      Submodule.Quotient.mk s := by
243	  haveI : Subsingleton
244	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
245	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
246	  haveI : Subsingleton
247	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
248	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
249	  apply ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).injective
250	  calc ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
251	        (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
252	      = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
253	          (((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
254	            ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
255	                (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
256	              ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule'
257	                  (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
258	                ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s)))) :=
259	        rfl
260	    _ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s := by
261	        rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
262	    _ = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
263	          (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) :=
264	        (MayerVietorisSquare.h1LinearEquiv_mk (S := X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov)
265	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) s).symm
266	
267	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map, inverse form: the inverse
268	bridge sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class. -/
269	lemma h1CokEquiv_symm_mk (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
270	    (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) =
271	      delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s := by
272	  apply (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁).injective
273	  rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, h1CokEquiv_delta]
274	
275	end Bridge

     9	/-!
    10	# Affine two-chart covers, and their pullback along the base-change projection
    11	
    12	An **affine two-chart cover** of a scheme `Y` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover`) is a pair of affine
    13	opens `V₀, V₁` covering `Y` whose overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is again affine. This file provides:
    14	
    15	* the structure `Scheme.AffineTwoCover`;
    16	* **existence** for the challenge curve: the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve
    17	  `C/k` admits an affine two-chart cover (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`), obtained
    18	  as the preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` under a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹`
    19	  (`exists_isFinite_toP1`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1`); the overlap is affine because it
    20	  is the preimage of the affine chart overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`;
    21	* **stability under base change**: an affine two-chart cover of `C.left` pulls back, along the
    22	  first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`, to an affine two-chart cover of
    23	  `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, for any `k`-algebra `R` (`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`).
    24	  The key input is that the first projection is an affine morphism: it is the base change of
    25	  `overSpec k R ⟶ Spec k` (itself affine, being a morphism between affine schemes) along
    26	  `C.hom` (`Over.isAffineHom_fst_left`), and preimages of affine opens under an affine
    27	  morphism are affine.
    28	
    29	## Main declarations
    30	
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover` — the structure.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve` — existence for the curve.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isAffineHom_fst_left` — the first projection of a base change along
    34	  an affine morphism is affine.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd` — the pullback of an affine two-chart
    36	  cover along the first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`.
    37	-/
    38	
    39	set_option autoImplicit false
    40	
    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    44	
    45	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    46	
    47	/-! ## The structure -/
    48	
    49	/-- An **affine two-chart cover** of a scheme `Y`: two affine opens `V₀, V₁` covering `Y`
    50	whose overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is again affine. -/
    51	structure Scheme.AffineTwoCover (Y : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
    52	  /-- The first chart. -/
    53	  V₀ : Y.Opens
    54	  /-- The second chart. -/
    55	  V₁ : Y.Opens
    56	  /-- The first chart is affine. -/
    57	  isAffineOpen₀ : IsAffineOpen V₀
    58	  /-- The second chart is affine. -/
    59	  isAffineOpen₁ : IsAffineOpen V₁
    60	  /-- The two charts cover `Y`. -/
    61	  sup_eq_top : V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤
    62	  /-- The overlap of the two charts is affine. -/
    63	  isAffineOpen_inf : IsAffineOpen (V₀ ⊓ V₁)
    64	
    65	/-- The overlap of the two charts of an affine two-chart cover is contained in the first
    66	chart. -/
    67	theorem Scheme.AffineTwoCover.inf_le_left {Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : Y.AffineTwoCover) :
    68	    D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₀ :=
    69	  _root_.inf_le_left
    70	
    71	/-- The overlap of the two charts of an affine two-chart cover is contained in the second
    72	chart. -/
    73	theorem Scheme.AffineTwoCover.inf_le_right {Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : Y.AffineTwoCover) :
    74	    D.V₀ ⊓ D.V₁ ≤ D.V₁ :=
    75	  _root_.inf_le_right
    76	
    77	/-! ## Existence: the two chart preimages of a finite map to the projective line -/
    78	
    79	section Existence
    80	
    81	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    82	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    83	
    84	/-- **Existence of an affine two-chart cover of the curve**: the smooth, proper,
    85	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` admits an affine two-chart cover, obtained as the
    86	preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` under a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹`
    87	(`exists_isFinite_toP1`). The charts are affine and cover `C.left`
    88	(`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`); the overlap is affine because
    89	it is the preimage of the affine chart overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` (`P1.isAffineOpen_overlap`), via
    90	`P1.chartOpen_inf` and preimage commuting with `⊓`. -/
    91	theorem Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve : Nonempty C.left.AffineTwoCover := by
    92	  obtain ⟨π, hfin, -⟩ := exists_isFinite_toP1 (C := C)
    93	  haveI := hfin
    94	  -- restated with the ambient scheme literally `P1 k` (as `P1.chartOpen` is stated), so that
    95	  -- `.preimage π` below unifies against `π : C.left ⟶ P1 k` without unfolding `P1`.
    96	  have hinf : IsAffineOpen (P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ P1.chartOpen k 1) := by
    97	    rw [P1.chartOpen_inf k]
    98	    exact P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k
    99	  refine ⟨{ V₀ := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0
   100	            V₁ := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1
   101	            isAffineOpen₀ := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0
   102	            isAffineOpen₁ := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1
   103	            sup_eq_top := preimage_chartOpen_sup π
   104	            isAffineOpen_inf := ?_ }⟩
   105	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf]
   106	  exact hinf.preimage π
   107	
   108	end Existence
   109	
   110	/-! ## Pullback along the base-change projection -/
   111	
   112	/-- **The first projection of a base change along an affine morphism is affine**: for `X, T`
   113	objects of `Over S`, `(fst X T).left` is (up to the defeq `Over.fst_left`/`Over.tensorObj_left`)
   114	the pullback of `T.hom` along `X.hom`, i.e. `Limits.pullback.fst X.hom T.hom`
   115	(`Over.isPullback_left`, flipped so that the affine leg `T.hom` lines up with the class field
   116	`IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback`); affineness is stable under base change
   117	(`isAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange`). -/
   118	instance Over.isAffineHom_fst_left {S : Scheme.{u}} (X T : Over S) [IsAffineHom T.hom] :
   119	    IsAffineHom (fst X T).left :=
   120	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsAffineHom) (Over.isPullback_left X T).flip ‹_›
   121

   139	/-- **Base change of an affine two-chart cover**: an affine two-chart cover `D` of `C.left`
   140	pulls back, along the first projection `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left ⟶ C.left`, to an affine
   141	two-chart cover of `(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, for any `k`-algebra `R`. The charts are the

   144	`overSpec k R ⟶ Spec k` is a morphism between affine schemes hence affine), preimage of an
   145	affine open under an affine morphism is affine, and preimage commutes with `⊔`, `⊓`, `⊤`. -/

     9	/-!
    10	# The tangent space of the Jacobian at the identity (W5-T5, the scalar-identity spine)
    11	
    12	The Wave-5 tangent statements phrased against the pinned representability datum
    13	`(d : JacobianData C)` (roadmap `AJCR.w5-av.t5`), assembling the generic kit of
    14	`Tangent/` into the two forms Wave 5 actually consumes:
    15	
    16	```
    17	Dual κ(e) (m_e/m_e²)  ≃  T_e(d.J)  ≃  ker (Pic⁰(Spec k[ε]) →* Pic⁰(Spec k))
    18	```
    19	
    20	and, under the **one** remaining numerical input, the frozen scalar identity
    21	`dim_κ(e) m_e/m_e² = genus C` together with its additive consequence
    22	`m_e/m_e² ≃+ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`.
    23	
    24	## The scalar-identity-first discipline (w5-worksheet D6), and what it buys
    25	
    26	The W12 lesson recorded in the worksheet is that dimension transport must go
    27	through **one** `finrank` identity, followed by **one** non-canonical `≃+` — not
    28	through a chain of additive equivalences each carrying its own linearity
    29	bookkeeping. This file is that discipline made structural:
    30	
    31	* `JacobianData.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` is the representability leg,
    32	  unconditional and sorry-free. It is a bijection of **sets**; it deliberately
    33	  does *not* claim to transport dimension (a bare `Equiv` cannot).
    34	* `JacobianData.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus` isolates the numerical
    35	  content as a **hypothesis** `hdim`. That hypothesis is what the T3/T4 chain must
    36	  deliver.
    37	* `JacobianData.nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1` then produces the additive
    38	  equivalence from the count, once.
    39	
    40	So the Wave-5 tangent keystone is, at HEAD, reduced to a statement about the
    41	`ε`-kernel of `pic0Functor` — **but note precisely which statement**. The
    42	`ε`-kernel *bijection* above is not enough on its own: it is a bijection of sets,
    43	and `finrank` does not transport along one. What `hdim` needs is the **semilinear
    44	comparison** — an additive equivalence plus the intertwining law across
    45	`κ(e) ≃+* k` — fed through `finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` (proved
    46	below, unconditionally). Stating T3/T4's target as a bare kernel bijection would
    47	leave the count unreachable; this is the same residue the AJC sibling isolated as
    48	`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`. See inbox I-0513.
    49	
    50	Note that the
    51	identity point of `d.J` needs no rationality hypothesis: it is the image of the
    52	group-object unit, hence a section, hence automatically `k`-rational
    53	(`bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section`).
    54	
    55	## Main declarations
    56	
    57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.identitySection` — the `k`-rational identity
    58	  point of `d.J`, with `identitySection_isSection`.
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.tangentSpaceCotangentDual` — `T_0(d.J)` is the
    60	  `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space at the identity.
    61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` — `T_0(d.J)` is
    62	  the `ε`-kernel of `pic0Functor C` (the representability leg, applied).
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_pic0Kernel` — the two
    64	  composed: the cotangent dual at the identity *is* the `ε`-kernel.
    65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace` — the
    66	  cotangent space at the identity is finite-dimensional (from
    67	  `d.locallyOfFiniteType`).
    68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` —
    69	  **unconditional**: `finrank` transports across a scalar *bijection* given an
    70	  additive equivalence and the intertwining law. The bridge that makes the count
    71	  reachable at all.
    72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus` /
    73	  `nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1` — the frozen scalar identity and its
    74	  additive consequence, each conditional on the T3/T4 semilinear comparison.
    75	
    76	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020);
    77	Milne, "Abelian varieties", Prop. 2.1.
    78	-/

    81	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    84	
    85	open CategoryTheory IsLocalRing Opposite

    87	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    88	
    89	namespace JacobianData
    90	
    91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    92	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    93	
    94	/-- **The identity point of the Jacobian.** The underlying scheme morphism
    95	`Spec k ⟶ d.J.left` of the group-object unit — the `k`-rational point at which
    96	Wave 5 computes the tangent space. -/
    97	noncomputable def identitySection (d : JacobianData C) : Spec (.of k) ⟶ d.J.left :=
    98	  letI := d.grpObj
    99	  GroupScheme.identitySection d.J
   100	
   101	/-- The identity point is a section of the structural morphism (the unit is a
   102	morphism of `Over (Spec k)` out of the monoidal unit). -/
   103	lemma identitySection_isSection (d : JacobianData C) :
   104	    d.identitySection ≫ d.J.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) :=
   105	  letI := d.grpObj
   106	  GroupScheme.identitySection_comp d.J
   107	
   108	/-- **The tangent space of the Jacobian at the identity, as a cotangent dual**
   109	(Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11, LHS). The pointed dual-number points of `d.J` at the
   110	identity form the `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space `m_e/m_e²`. No
   111	rationality hypothesis is needed: the identity point is a section, hence
   112	automatically `k`-rational. -/
   113	noncomputable def tangentSpaceCotangentDual (d : JacobianData C) :
   114	    pointedDualNumberPoints d.J d.identitySection ≃
   115	      Module.Dual
   116	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   117	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))) :=
   118	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
   119	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
   120	  overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual d.J (d.identitySection_isSection)
   121	    (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim _ _))
   122	
   123	/-- **The representability leg, applied** (Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11): the tangent
   124	space of `d.J` at the identity is the **kernel** of the restriction
   125	homomorphism
   126	
   127	```
   128	Pic⁰_{C/k}(Spec k[ε]) →* Pic⁰_{C/k}(Spec k)
   129	```
   130	
   131	along the `ε ↦ 0` point. Immediate from `pointedDualNumberPointsEquivKer` at the
   132	pinned datum `d.rep`, whose functor is `pic0Functor C` composed with the
   133	forgetful functors — note the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` typing of `rep` is exactly what
   134	makes the group-valued kernel meaningful, and `JacobianData` owns that massage.
   135	
   136	⚠ A bijection of **sets**: it does not transport `finrank`. That is the point of
   137	the scalar-identity-first discipline — see the module docstring. -/
   138	noncomputable def tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel (d : JacobianData C) :
   139	    pointedDualNumberPoints d.J d.identitySection ≃
   140	      {a : (pic0Functor C).obj (op (overDualNumber k)) //
   141	        ((pic0Functor C).map (overDualNumberZero k).op).hom a = 1} :=
   142	  pointedDualNumberPointsEquivKer d.J (pic0Functor C) d.rep d.identitySection_isSection
   143	
   144	/-- **The two legs composed**: the `κ(e)`-linear dual of the cotangent space at
   145	the identity of `d.J` *is* the `ε`-kernel of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`. This is the statement
   146	the T3/T4 chain computes against, and the one whose dimension T5 counts. -/
   147	noncomputable def cotangentSpaceDual_equiv_pic0Kernel (d : JacobianData C) :
   148	    Module.Dual
   149	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   150	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   151	      ≃ {a : (pic0Functor C).obj (op (overDualNumber k)) //
   152	          ((pic0Functor C).map (overDualNumberZero k).op).hom a = 1} :=
   153	  d.tangentSpaceCotangentDual.symm.trans d.tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel
   154	
   155	/-- **Finite-dimensionality of the cotangent space at the identity.** The
   156	Jacobian is locally of finite type over `k` by the datum's certificate, hence
   157	locally Noetherian, so `m_e/m_e²` is a finite-dimensional `κ(e)`-vector space —
   158	the input any dimension count needs. -/
   159	theorem finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace (d : JacobianData C) :
   160	    FiniteDimensional
   161	      (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   162	      (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))) :=
   163	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   164	  letI : IsLocallyNoetherian d.J.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian d.J.hom
   165	  inferInstance
   166	
   167	/-! ## The frozen scalar identity, and the bridge T3/T4 must actually cross
   168	
   169	Everything above is unconditional. What follows carries the numerical input as an
   170	explicit hypothesis, named once:
   171	
   172	```
   173	hdim : Module.finrank κ(e) (m_e/m_e²) = genus C
   174	```
   175	
   176	Keeping it a hypothesis rather than a `sorry` is the w5-worksheet §0(4) rule
   177	(never register a staged fact).
   178	
   179	**What `hdim` needs, stated precisely — the `ε`-kernel bijection alone is NOT
   180	enough.** `tangentSpaceEquivPic0Kernel` is a bijection of *sets* (it says so on
   181	its own docstring) and a bare `Equiv` does not determine `finrank`. So T3/T4's
   182	kernel computation does not by itself give `hdim`: additionally required is an
   183	**additive** equivalence together with the intertwining law across the
   184	residue-field bijection `κ(e) → k`, because the two sides are modules over
   185	genuinely different rings — neither `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq` nor a
   186	`restrictScalars` argument applies.
   187	
   188	`finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul` below is exactly that bridge, and it
   189	is unconditional. With it in hand the residual obligation on T3/T4 is the
   190	**semilinear comparison**: a scalar bijection `i`, an additive equivalence `j`
   191	from `Dual κ(e) (m_e/m_e²)` to `H¹(C,𝒪)`, and `j (r • x) = i r • j x`. That is
   192	the honest target to state T3/T4 against — and it is the same residue the AJC
   193	sibling isolated (`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`), which is why
   194	porting the generic kit without this bridge would have left the count
   195	unreachable. Found by fresh-context review; see inbox I-0513. -/
   196	
   197	/-- **`finrank` across a scalar bijection** (the linearity bridge the Wave-5
   198	count needs, and the reason the `ε`-kernel *set* bijection is insufficient on its
   199	own). If `i : R → R'` is a bijection of scalars, `j : M ≃+ M₁` an additive
   200	equivalence, and the two intertwine (`j (r • m) = i r • j m`), then `M` and `M₁`
   201	have equal `finrank` over their respective rings.
   202	
   203	`i` need only be a **bijection**, not a ring homomorphism, and the module
   204	structures live over genuinely different rings — which is precisely the situation
   205	of the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 count, comparing a `κ(e)`-dimension with a
   206	`k`-dimension across `κ(e) ≃+* k`. Mathlib has this at the level of
   207	`Module.rank` (`rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv`) but not in `finrank` form; this is the
   208	`Module.finrank = toNat ∘ Module.rank` unfolding of it. -/
   209	theorem finrank_eq_of_addEquiv_of_bijective_smul
   210	    {R : Type*} {R' : Type*} {M M₁ : Type v} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
   211	    [Semiring R'] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [Module R' M₁]
   212	    (i : R → R') (j : M ≃+ M₁) (hi : Function.Bijective i)
   213	    (hc : ∀ (r : R) (m : M), j (r • m) = i r • j m) :
   214	    Module.finrank R M = Module.finrank R' M₁ := by
   215	  unfold Module.finrank
   216	  rw [rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv i j hi hc]
   217	
   218	variable (d : JacobianData C)
   219	
   220	/-- **The frozen scalar identity** `dim_κ(e) T₀(d.J) = genus C`, conditional on
   221	the T3/T4 count. Stated in cotangent form: since `T₀(d.J)` is by
   222	`tangentSpaceCotangentDual` the `κ(e)`-linear dual of `m_e/m_e²` and the latter
   223	is finite-dimensional (`finiteDimensional_cotangentSpace`), the dual has the same
   224	dimension, so this single `finrank` equation *is* the Wave-5 dimension
   225	statement — no further transport is needed or wanted (w5-worksheet D6).
   226	
   227	The hypothesis is exactly what T3/T4 produce; nothing else in Wave 5 needs the
   228	`ε`-kernel in any other form. -/
   229	theorem finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_genus
   230	    (hdim : Module.finrank
   231	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   232	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   233	      = genus C) :
   234	    Module.finrank
   235	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   236	        (Module.Dual
   237	          (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   238	          (CotangentSpace
   239	            (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))))
   240	      = genus C := by
   241	  rw [Subspace.dual_finrank_eq]
   242	  exact hdim
   243	
   244	/-- **The Wave-5 tangent keystone, additively** (Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11): the
   245	cotangent space at the identity of `d.J` is additively isomorphic to
   246	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, given the scalar identity. This is the "one non-canonical `≃+`
   247	after one `finrank` identity" of the D6 discipline: the equivalence is produced
   248	*once*, by choosing bases on both sides and transporting along `κ(e) ≃+* k`
   249	(`nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq`), and it is `Nonempty` because
   250	that choice is not canonical.
   251	
   252	`genus C` is by definition `finrank k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Challenge.lean`), so the
   253	hypothesis really is the dimension comparison of the two sides. -/
   254	theorem nonempty_cotangentSpace_addEquiv_h1
   255	    [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
   256	    (hdim : Module.finrank
   257	        (ResidueField (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   258	        (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default)))
   259	      = genus C) :
   260	    Nonempty
   261	      (CotangentSpace (d.J.left.presheaf.stalk (d.identitySection.base default))
   262	        ≃+ Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   263	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   264	  nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq d.J d.identitySection_isSection
   265	    (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) hdim
   266	
   267	end JacobianData

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafDatumBaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafCongr
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorClass

/-!
# The Čech Picard class of a gluing cocycle (DAT-1, stage 1e — the class law)

The class law of `informal/spec-dat-1.md` stage (1e): a gluing cocycle on pieces
`U : J → X.Opens` determines a class in the definitional Picard group
`Scheme.CechPic` on every pointed cover subordinated to the pieces, independently of
the subordination; for the pinned basic-open cocycle datum the pieces cover the
relative curve, giving **the** class of the datum, natural in the test ring.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSubordCocycle` — the unit Čech 1-cocycle induced on a
  pointed cover `𝒲` subordinated to the pieces (`σ : X → J`,
  `hσ : 𝒲.opens x ≤ U (σ x)`): pair values the restricted transition units.
* `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq` — **subordination independence**: any two subordinated
  pointed covers give the same `CechPic` class (restrict to the common refinement; the
  two restricted cocycles are cohomologous through the `0`-cochain
  `x ↦ g (σ' x) (σ x)`, by the cocycle law).
* `gluedSubordCocycle_isCohomologous_of_coboundary` — cohomologous gluing cocycles
  (`Scheme.IsGluingCoboundary`) induce cohomologous subordinated cocycles, hence equal
  classes (`gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq_of_coboundary`) — the class-level face of the
  landed sheaf-level transport `gluedSheafCongr`.
* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass` — the class of the pinned datum (worksheet
  §3.2), on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; `cechPicClass_eq_mk` re-expresses it
  on **any** subordinated pointed cover (the interface the stage-(1f) extraction and
  DAT-3 consume).
* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_baseChange` — **naturality in the test ring**:
  the class of the base-changed datum is the `CechPic.map`-pullback of the class along
  `relCurveMap C B B'`.
-/

    10	/-!
    11	# Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism, and the dictionary
    12	
    13	For an affine scheme `X` this file proves surjectivity of the descent homomorphism
    14	`CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` and assembles the full
    15	**Čech–Picard dictionary**
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic : X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`
    18	
    19	— the isomorphism between the definitional Čech Picard group on pointed Zariski covers
    20	and mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules (the TODO of
    21	`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`: "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").
    22	
    23	The route: an invertible module `N` over `Γ(X, ⊤)` trivializes on the basic open of
    24	some section outside every prime, so the trivializing sections span the unit ideal
    25	(`Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`) and their basic opens cover `X`.  A
    26	choice of one trivializing basic neighborhood per point is a `TrivializingFamily`; the
    27	transition units of its trivializations (`Module.transitionUnit`) form a unit Čech
    28	cocycle on the associated pointed cover.  Along any finite basic refinement the
    29	restricted cover cocycle is the transition cocycle of the pushed-forward
    30	trivializations, so its descended module is `N` itself
    31	(`IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle`), and `toPic` hits the class
    32	of `N`.
    33	-/

    35	set_option autoImplicit false

    37	universe u

    48	/-! ## Trivializing families -/
    49	
    50	/-- A pointed trivializing family for a module `N` over the global sections of `X`: one
    51	section per point, whose basic open contains the point and carries a trivialization of
    52	the base change of `N`.  Invertible modules over affine schemes always admit one
    53	(`TrivializingFamily.nonempty`). -/
    54	structure TrivializingFamily (X : Scheme.{u}) (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N]
    55	    [Module Γ(X, ⊤) N] : Type u where
    56	  /-- The trivializing section at a point. -/
    57	  sec : X → Γ(X, ⊤)
    58	  /-- Each point lies in the basic open of its section. -/
    59	  mem_basicOpen : ∀ x, x ∈ X.basicOpen (sec x)
    60	  /-- The chosen trivialization of `N` over the basic open. -/
    61	  triv : ∀ x, (Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x)) ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)
    62	    ≃ₗ[Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))] Γ(X, X.basicOpen (sec x))
    63

    67	
    68	/-- Every invertible module over the global sections of an affine scheme admits a
    69	trivializing family: the trivializing sections span the unit ideal, so their basic
    70	opens cover `X`. -/
    71	theorem nonempty [IsAffine X] [Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) N] :
    72	    Nonempty (TrivializingFamily X N) := by
    73	  have hcover :
    74	      (⨆ f : {f : Γ(X, ⊤) | ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra Γ(X, ⊤) S],
    75	          IsLocalization.Away f S → Module.Free S (S ⊗[Γ(X, ⊤)] N)},
    76	        X.basicOpen f.1) = ⊤ :=

    78	      (Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top N)

    11	
    12	The étale sheafification of the relative Picard functor is computed over *affine* test
    13	objects, where a test object is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra `A` (the landed

    19	  (`overSpecMap_id`, `overSpecMap_comp`).
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap C f`: restriction of relative Picard classes along
    21	  `Spec f`, a group homomorphism `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* relPic C (overSpec k B)`,
    22	  covariantly functorial in the algebra (`relPicAlgMap_id`, `relPicAlgMap_comp`).

    24	The étale plus construction (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`) consumes only this interface: descent
    25	classes on an étale cover are an equalizer of two `relPicAlgMap`s, and all refinement

# W5-T4 worksheet — the étale-plus/Zariski kernel crossing at `k[ε]` (risk R1)

**RATIFIED — BINDING (orchestrator, 2026-07-17 night session).** Route (ii) is adopted
as recommended below; route (i) remains the documented fallback. The pending t3 brick
(AJCR.w5-av.t3) is RE-SCOPED to T4-b (the coefficient-natural ε-kernel over finite
products of fields) — the roadmap item carries the amendment. The whole T/S cluster
(t1, t3/T4-b, t4-a..e, t5, s1, s2, s3) is assigned to the dedicated Wave-5 smoothness
session (third fleet); see `w5-worksheet.md` §3 addendum for the division of labor.

*Produced 2026-07-17 by the read-only design-probe lane w5-t4-probe (AJCR.w5-av.t4), per
w5-worksheet §1 D4 ("T4 WORKSHEET-FIRST") and w5-recon §3.1 G-W5-T4 / §5 R1 / §5 R3. No
file outside `informal/` touched; no build run; every claim below re-verified against the
pinned mathlib checkout (`.lake-packages/mathlib`, v4.31.0, `fabf563a7c9…`) and the landed
Lean tree at probe time. Mathlib paths are under `Mathlib/`, project paths under
`AlgebraicJacobian/`.*

---

## §0 Verdict in one line

**Recommend route (ii)** — the kernel-level cancellation over `k`, run at every field base
`K/k` uniformly — because the probe found that (a) the "Artin-local splitting" both routes
feared needs **no henselian machinery at all** (the thickening is square-zero, so mathlib's
`FormallyEtale`/`FormallySmooth` square-zero lifting plus the étale-over-a-field structure
theorem do the whole cover-refinement job), (b) the "Hilbert-90-flavoured" cancellation
**dissolves into the already-landed module-level Amitsur exactness** of `Descent/`
(after the T2 truncated-exp linearization the descent condition is additive, and degree-≤1
additive Amitsur exactness is `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub`,
`Descent/ModuleDescent.lean:247` — no unit-cocycle cancellation, no Galois theory), and
(c) route (i)'s close of the frozen numeral is **structurally coupled to the R3 mathlib
gap** (no rel-dim descent exists; appendix §5), whereas route (ii) hands T5 the k-side
count `ker(pic0(k[ε]) → pic0(k)) ≃+ H¹(C,𝒪)` on the nose, with the `k̄`-side instance and
the tangent base-change square falling out of the same uniform statement. Route (i)
survives verbatim as the documented fallback: it is the separably-closed degenerate case
of route (ii)'s bricks.

The single hardest brick on the recommended route is **T4-b** (§3): the
coefficient-natural ε-kernel isomorphism
`ker(relPic C (A[ε]) → relPic C (A)) ≃+ H¹(C,𝒪) ⊗[k] A`, natural in a k-algebra `A`
ranging over finite products of fields — a re-scope of the pending t3 brick (t3 is
unstarted, so this is a scope amendment, not rework). **Orchestrator action needed:
ratify the t3 re-scope before the t3 lane launches.**

---

## §1 Probe evidence — mathlib inventory (all re-verified this session)

### 1(a) `HenselianLocalRing`: an island; nothing usable, and nothing needed

- `HenselianLocalRing` class: `RingTheory/Henselian.lean:108`; `HenselianRing R I`
  (:94); `HenselianLocalRing.TFAE` (:119, simple-root lifting forms only);
  `Field.henselian` (:114); quotient instance (:154);
  `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing` (:170).
- **Zero consumers**: `grep -rn Henselian` over the pinned checkout hits *no file other
  than `RingTheory/Henselian.lean` itself*. There is no étale-cover splitting, no
  "finite algebra over henselian local = product of local rings", no idempotent lifting
  stated over henselian rings, no section-existence statement. The R1 fear "the
  splitting brick is unverified in mathlib" is confirmed: **it is absent**.
- Adjacent structure theory that does exist: idempotent lifting along *nilpotent*
  kernels — `exists_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent`
  (`RingTheory/Idempotents.lean:248`, plus the complete-orthogonal-family lifting
  machinery in the same file); reduced Artinian decomposition `IsArtinianRing.equivPi :
  R ≃ₐ[R] Π (I : MaximalSpectrum R), R ⧸ I.asIdeal` (`RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:623`).
- **Why none of this matters for T4**: the project's covers are
  `Algebra.Etale A B` = `FormallyEtale` + `FinitePresentation`
  (`RingTheory/Etale/Basic.lean:213`; project `Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:64-87`), and the
  test thickening `K[ε] → K` has square-zero kernel. So the entire "henselian lifting"
  content collapses to ONE application of the square-zero lifting API:
  `Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp_surjective (I : Ideal B) (hI : I ^ 2 = ⊥)`
  (`RingTheory/Smooth/Basic.lean:83`) / `Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective`
  (`RingTheory/Etale/Basic.lean:77`). No henselian induction, no idempotents.

### 1(b) Étale algebra structure: the field-level structure theory is a complete gift

- `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod` (`RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean:271`): `A/K`
  étale ⟺ `A ≃ₐ[K] Π i, Ai i` finite product of finite separable field extensions.
  (Formally-étale version at :194; the project already consumes it:
  `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`, `Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`.)
- `Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed` (`Etale/Field.lean:217`): over a
  separably closed `K`, an étale algebra is `≃ₐ[K] (PrimeSpectrum A → K)` — the
  **split** case; with `IsSepClosed.algebraMap_bijective`
  (`FieldTheory/IsSepClosed.lean:213`) and `IsSepClosed.of_isAlgClosed` (:72).
- Base change and composition: `Algebra.Etale.baseChange` instance
  (`Etale/Basic.lean:249`), `Algebra.Etale.comp` (:244) — so
  `(EtaleCover.ofField L).baseChange (K[ε])` is a legal cover of `K[ε]` with carrier
  `K[ε] ⊗[K] L` through the landed `EtaleCover.baseChange` (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:238`).
- Standard-étale presentations exist (`RingTheory/Etale/StandardEtale.lean`;
  `Algebra.IsEtaleAt.exists_isStandardEtale`,
  `RingTheory/Unramified/LocalStructure.lean:374`;
  fiber-splitting étale neighborhoods of finite algebras,
  `RingTheory/Etale/QuasiFinite.lean:378`) — all spectrum-local *constructions of covers*,
  none produces sections over a local base. **Not needed** on either route.
- "étale + local + henselian ⇒ has a section": **absent**; replaced by 1(a)'s
  square-zero observation.

### 1(c) Hilbert 90 / unit descent: mathlib has the wrong shape; the project has the right one

- Mathlib's Hilbert 90 is Galois-cohomological only:
  `groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units`
  (`RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Hilbert90.lean:84`, norm forms
  :134/:172). No Amitsur/étale-cover form, no Galois↔Amitsur bridge. Unusable here
  without a new bridge campaign — **do not route through it**.
- Mathlib faithfully-flat descent of ring-hom properties:
  injective/surjective/bijective (`RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Descent.lean:31-72`).
  No units-of-covers statements.
- **Project-landed (the decisive assets)**, `Descent/`:
  - `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub` (`Descent/ModuleDescent.lean:247`):
    degree-≤1 **Amitsur exactness for an arbitrary `A`-module `N`** along faithfully
    flat `A → B`, i.e. exactness of `N → B ⊗[A] N → (coaction − 1⊗–)`; unit-of-descent
    iso `DescentDatum.unitEquiv` (:269).
  - `Module.FaithfullyFlat.existsUnique_tmul_one_eq` (`Descent/AmitsurEqualizer.lean:36`):
    the two-coprojection **face form** of degree-0 exactness — stated for an *algebra*
    coefficient `S₀`; the module-coefficient face form is a ~30-line transport of
    :247 in exactly the pattern this file already executes (brick T4-c).
  - Cocycle-level unit descent with the full `picClass` calculus incl.
    `picClass_eq_one_iff` (`Descent/UnitDescent.lean`) — available but **not needed**:
    route (ii) never descends a unit cocycle, only an additive H¹ element.
- Also landed and consumed by the close: `PicEtAff.unit_injective` — (C1), unconditional
  over every k-algebra test (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361-365`); the keystone
  `relPicAlgMap_congr` (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean:161`); `mapAlg` restriction with
  cover-base-change transport `descentBaseChange` (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean:275, :72`);
  the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` (`Picard/PicEt.lean:235`);
  `Over.sectionsBaseChange` for any k-algebra coefficient
  (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`, docstring reserves `A = k[ε]` for this lane).

### 1(d) The R3 side probe — answered; details in appendix §5

`HasRingHomProperty.descendsAlong_flat` (`AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/FlatDescent.lean:156`)
does **NOT** instantiate at `Locally (IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n)` as-is: of
its three requirements, two are present and the third is a genuine mathlib absence
(`RingHom.CodescendsAlong (Locally (IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n))
RingHom.FaithfullyFlat`), though the probe found all raw material to build it as an [M]
brick. See §5.

---

## §2 Route assessment against the landed tree

Both routes cross the same bridge: the represented kernel lives in `picEt`/`PicEtAff`-land
(via `d.rep` + `picEtAffineEquiv`), T3's lives in `relPic`-land, and the landed dictionary
(`PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section`, `Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:186`) crosses only at
sectioned field tests. The crossing at a dual-number test = "the unit is bijective on the
ε-kernel". Injectivity is landed ((C1), any test). **Only surjectivity onto the ε-kernel
is open.**

A structural fact the probe surfaced, which reframes the comparison: **route (i) does not
avoid generalizing T3 beyond coefficient `k`.** Computing `ker(relPic(k̄[ε]) → relPic(k̄))`
is the T2/T3 engine with coefficient algebra `A = k̄` (section rings `B ⊗[k] k̄`, via
`Over.sectionsBaseChange`), not the currently-scoped `A = k` statement. Both routes
therefore amend t3; they differ only in *how far*.

### Route (i) — k̄-side splitting + comparison square. Enumerated needs:

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle
7	
8	/-!
9	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
10	
11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
12	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
13	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
14	stabilized along the refinement preorder.
15	
16	## Main declarations
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
19	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
20	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
21	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
23	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
24	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
26	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
27	-/
28	
29	set_option autoImplicit false
30	
31	universe u
32	
33	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
34	
35	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
36	
37	namespace Scheme
38	
39	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
40	
41	/-! ## The Picard group  -/
42	
43	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
44	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
46	  iseqv := by
47	    constructor
48	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
50	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
51	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
52	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
53	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
54	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
55	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
56	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'
57	
58	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
59	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/

/-!
# Unit-valued Čech cocycles on pointed covers and their pullback

This file sets up the cocycle-level substrate of the Čech Picard group
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic`):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PointedCover`: one open per point, containing it; a
  `SemilatticeInf` with an `OrderTop`, refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`,
  and pullback along a morphism of schemes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsCocycle`, `Scheme.unitsH1`: unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles
  and `H¹` on a pointed cover; `Scheme.unitsRes`: restriction along a refinement, a group
  homomorphism, strictly functorial (`unitsRes_unitsRes`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsEvInf`, `Scheme.unitsRestrict`: the pair values of a
  unit cocycle and restriction of unit sections, retyped through `Γ(X, U)ˣ`. Statements
  phrased through these are honestly `Γ`-typed, so `rw`/`simp` work on them; goals arising
  from the `OneCochain` field types (whose carriers go through `unitsPresheaf.obj`) are
  closed against them by `exact` — the two spellings are definitionally equal.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle`, `Hom.pullbackUnitsH1`: pullback of
  unit cocycles and their `H¹` classes along a morphism of schemes, compatible with
  restriction (`unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1`) — the substrate for `CechPic.map`.

The file starts with generic `evInf` algebra for `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups`
(values of cochains/cocycles at binary infima commute with `1`, `*`, `⁻¹`); it lives here
only because `CechH1.lean` is at the file-size cap, and should move alongside
`OneCochain.evInf` when that file is split for a mathlib PR.
-/

    25	étale separatedness (arbitrary `A`), the dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and the
    26	χ-ledger under field extension (`A = K`). Hence the statements are for an arbitrary
    27	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and `V` is allowed to be any quasi-compact quasi-separated
    28	open (e.g. the intersection of two affines of the curve), not just an affine one.

    31	
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left` — the bridge: for `X T : Over S`, the scheme-level
    33	  square `(fst X T).left, (snd X T).left, X.hom, T.hom` is a pullback.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A` — `Spec A` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`, together with

    44	  needs `[Flat T.hom]`).
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections` — the same square with the
    46	  `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)`/`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` corners replaced by `k` and `A`.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.InvertibleLocalTrivialization

/-!
# Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism, and the dictionary

For an affine scheme `X` this file proves surjectivity of the descent homomorphism
`CechPic.toPic : X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)` and assembles the full
**Čech–Picard dictionary**

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPicEquivPic : X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`

— the isomorphism between the definitional Čech Picard group on pointed Zariski covers
and mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules (the TODO of
`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`: "exhibit isomorphism with `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`").

The route: an invertible module `N` over `Γ(X, ⊤)` trivializes on the basic open of
some section outside every prime, so the trivializing sections span the unit ideal
(`Module.Invertible.span_tensor_free_eq_top`) and their basic opens cover `X`.  A
choice of one trivializing basic neighborhood per point is a `TrivializingFamily`; the
transition units of its trivializations (`Module.transitionUnit`) form a unit Čech
cocycle on the associated pointed cover.  Along any finite basic refinement the
restricted cover cocycle is the transition cocycle of the pushed-forward
trivializations, so its descended module is `N` itself
(`IsLocalization.AwayCover.picClass_trivializationCocycle`), and `toPic` hits the class
of `N`.
-/

open TensorProduct

/-! ## Trivializing families -/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic

/-!
# Refinement injectivity for the unit Čech `H¹`

In degree one, Čech cohomology classes on a cover embed into those on any refinement:
for pointed covers `𝒲 ≤ 𝒰` of a scheme `X`, the restriction map
`unitsRes : X.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 𝒲` is **injective**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsRes_injective`). Consequently the refinement colimit
`Scheme.CechPic` is a colimit of injections: a class `CechPic.mk 𝒰 a` is trivial iff `a`
is already trivial on `𝒰` (`CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`), and `CechPic.mk 𝒰` is injective
(`CechPic.mk_injective`) — the classical statement `Ȟ¹(𝒰, 𝒪^*) ↪ Pic(X)`.

Mathematically: suppose the restriction to `𝒲` of a unit cocycle `γ` on `𝒰` is the
coboundary of a family of units `α z ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒲 z)`. The comparison sections
`α z ⋅ γ(i,z)⁻¹ ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i ⊓ 𝒲 z)` agree on overlaps — by the cocycle identity for `γ`
and the coboundary relation for `α` — hence glue, the units presheaf being a sheaf, to a
unit `β i ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 i)`; the family `β` exhibits `γ` as a coboundary on `𝒰` itself.

This file also provides the sheaf-theoretic substrate as reusable API: gluing
(`Scheme.exists_unitsRestrict_eq`) and separation (`Scheme.unitsRestrict_eq_of_locally_eq`)
for unit sections, together with the composition law `unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict`.

Refinement injectivity is the "fiberwise cocycle glue" of the separatedness ledger
(design §4.4) in reusable form; it is consumed by brick 3 (`Over.prPullback_injective`,
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Separatedness`) and by the Zariski-sheaf-on-affines corollary
of the étale-separatedness theorem (C1).
-/
